definition_en: to put a name or a fact on an official list; to show a feeling or a measurement; an official list or book of records
core_image: 前台一本摊开的厚本子，笔搁在刚写下的一行旁
scene: 前台摊着一本厚厚的登记簿，笔还搁在刚写下的那一行旁边。All visitors must register at the front desk before entering the lab.
sceneCN: 这里 register 是「登记」（第 1 个义项：把名字写进正式名册）；句意为所有访客进入实验室前都必须在前台登记。画面里可留意：摊开的本子、搁在行旁的笔。

senses.title: To put on an official list
senses.definition: to record a name, a fact, or an event in an official book or system
senses.definitionCN: 把姓名、事实或事件记入正式的册子或系统
senses.example: All visitors must register at the front desk before entering the lab.
senses.exampleCN: 所有访客进入实验室前都必须在前台登记。
senses.why: The Latin word behind it means things carried back and written down, so the act is first of all a matter of putting a record in place.
senses.whyCN: 其背后的拉丁词意为「被带回并记下的事物」，所以这个动作首先是「把记录安置好」。

senses.title: To show a sign
senses.definition: to show a feeling or a measurement without words
senses.definitionCN: 不用言语地显示出某种情绪或读数
senses.example: Her face registered surprise before she could hide it.
senses.exampleCN: 她还没来得及掩饰，脸上已显出惊讶。
senses.why: A face or a dial does what a ledger does: it records a fact where others can read it.
senses.whyCN: 面孔或表盘做的事和账簿一样：把事实记录下来，让别人读得到。

senses.title: An official list
senses.definition: a book or a roll in which names and facts are officially kept
senses.definitionCN: 正式保存姓名与事实的册子或名册
senses.example: The clerk ran a finger down the register until she found the name.
senses.exampleCN: 职员用手指沿着登记簿往下划，直到找到那个名字。
senses.why: The noun names the object that holds the records, and it is often the oldest sense of the family.
senses.whyCN: 名词命名保存记录的那个物件，这往往是这个词族最古老的一义。

intro.en: Register comes from a Latin word for things written down: what was carried back and set in a book became the book itself.
intro.cn: register 出自拉丁语中「被记下之事」的说法：被带回并写进册子的东西，后来就成了那本册子。

items.en: Gerere meant to carry, bear, or conduct, and it built many verbs of managing and recording.
items.cn: gerere 意为携带、承载或进行，构成了许多表管理与记录的动词。

items.en: Regerere joined re-, back, with gerere and meant to carry back or set down in writing.
items.cn: regerere 由 re-（往回）与 gerere 组成，意为带回或记录在案。

items.en: Regesta were the things recorded, and the word named collections of written entries.
items.cn: regesta 指被记录下来的事，这个词用来指书面条目的汇编。

items.en: Medieval Latin registrum named the book that held such entries, and Old French registre passed it on.
items.cn: 中世纪拉丁语 registrum 指保存这些条目的册子，古法语 registre 把它传了下去。

items.en: English extended the verb from writing in a book to any clear outward sign, such as a face or a dial.
items.cn: 英语把这个动词从「写进册子」扩展到任何清楚的外在迹象，例如面孔或表盘。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same recording family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of listing and noting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「记录」词族的词；近义组收表示列入与记下的动词。

entries.definition: A place or book of records.
To put a name on a list.
To set down in writing or sound.
To enter details in a regular record.
To join by writing your name.

normalIntro.en: The word is a book that carries names: to register is to put your name where it can be carried and read.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一本承载姓名的册子：登记就是把名字放到能被保存和读到的地方。

normal.en: Register for a course means to put your name on its list.
normal.cn: register for a course 指把名字写进这门课的名单。

normal.en: A hotel register is the book every guest signs.
normal.cn: hotel register 是每位客人签名的本子。

normal.en: A face can register surprise as clearly as a page records it.
normal.cn: 面孔能显出惊讶，就像纸页能记下惊讶一样清楚。

normal.en: Registration is the noun, registrar the person who keeps the book.
normal.cn: registration 是名词，registrar 是保管册子的人。

normal.en: To register a complaint is to make it official, not casual.
normal.cn: register a complaint 指正式提出，而不是随口一说。

abstract.en: To be registered is to be counted, and to be counted is to be seen.
abstract.cn: 被登记就是被数到，被数到就是被看见。

abstract.en: A register is a promise that the past will still be there tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 登记簿是一个承诺：过去在明天仍然存在。

abstract.en: What a society registers tells you what it fears to lose.
abstract.cn: 一个社会登记什么，就说明它害怕失去什么。

examples.en: All visitors must register at the front desk before entering the lab.
examples.cn: 所有访客进入实验室前都必须在前台登记。

examples.en: Her face registered surprise before she could hide it.
examples.cn: 她还没来得及掩饰，脸上已显出惊讶。

examples.en: The clerk ran a finger down the register until she found the name.
examples.cn: 职员用手指沿着登记簿往下划，直到找到那个名字。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回）加 gest（携带、记下）：把名字带回去记在本子上，就是登记；数字与表情被记下来，就是显示。

root: 拉丁 gerere（携带、进行）→ regerere（带回、记录）→ regesta（被记下之事）→ 中世纪拉丁 registrum（登记簿）→ 英语 register；同族有 registration、registrar、registry。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a written record; the senses move from the act of entering a name, to any clear outward sign, to the book that holds the entries.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「写下的记录」；义项从写下名字的动作，到任何清楚的外在迹象，再到保存条目的册子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick ledger open at the desk, a pen resting beside the newest line.
core.cn: 核心意象：前台一本摊开的厚本子，笔搁在刚写下的一行旁。

branches.en: a visitor signing at the desk
branches.cn: 在前台签名的访客

branches.en: surprise crossing a face
branches.cn: 掠过脸上的惊讶

branches.en: a finger sliding down a page
branches.cn: 顺着纸页往下滑的手指

branches.en: a name written and a name found
branches.cn: 写下的名字与被找到的名字

branches.en: signs noted as facts are noted
branches.cn: 迹象被记下，如同事实被记下

intro.en: A Latin verb of carrying takes a prefix of return, and what is carried back and written down gives its name to the book.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「携带」动词接上表返回的前缀，被带回并写下的东西，把自己的名字给了那本书。

latinIntro.en: The base is gerere, to carry; re- means back, and -strum marks the means or the place.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 gerere（携带）；re- 表「往回」，-strum 标记工具或场所。

definition_zh: 登记；注册；登记人数；读数
definition_en: the act of recording a name on an official list; the number of people recorded; the display shown by an instrument
core_image: 门口长桌上排着一叠待填的表格和一支笔
scene: 会场门口的长桌上，摆着一叠待填的表格和一支用绳子系住的笔。Registration closes on Friday at noon.
sceneCN: 这里 registration 是「登记报名」（第 1 个义项：把名字记入名册这一行为）；句意为报名在周五中午截止。画面里可留意：一叠表格、系着绳子的笔。

pos.zh: 登记；注册；登记人数；读数

senses.title: The act of registering
senses.definition: the process of putting a name or a fact on an official list
senses.definitionCN: 把姓名或事实记入正式名册的过程
senses.example: Registration closes on Friday at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 报名在周五中午截止。
senses.why: The noun of action names the whole procedure, from the blank form to the name finally written down.
senses.whyCN: 这个表行为的名词命名整套程序，从空白表格一直到终于写下的名字。

senses.title: The number recorded
senses.definition: the total number of people who have registered for something
senses.definitionCN: 为某事登记在册的总人数
senses.example: A registration of over three hundred made the hall feel small.
senses.exampleCN: 登记人数超过三百，让这个大厅显得小了。
senses.why: Once a list has been filled, it can be counted, and the count itself takes the same name.
senses.whyCN: 名单一旦填满就可以点数，而点出的数目也用同一个名字。

senses.title: A reading on a dial
senses.definition: the figure or position shown by a measuring instrument
senses.definitionCN: 测量仪器显示出的数字或位置
senses.example: The gauge gave a steady registration of twenty degrees.
senses.exampleCN: 仪表稳定地显示二十度。
senses.why: An instrument records a fact just as a book does, so its display is also called a registration.
senses.whyCN: 仪器记录事实的方式和册子一样，所以它的显示也被称作 registration。

intro.en: Registration is the noun of register: the same carrying back into a book now names the procedure, the count, and the reading.
intro.cn: registration 是 register 的名词：同一种「带回册子」的动作，如今命名程序、人数与读数。

items.en: Regesta were things written down, the base of the whole recording family.
items.cn: regesta 指被写下的事物，是整个「记录」词族的基础。

items.en: Registrum named the book of entries, and its verb registrare named the act of entering.
items.cn: registrum 指条目簿，其动词 registrare 指登记这一动作。

items.en: Old French registre and its verb passed into English as register.
items.cn: 古法语 registre 及其动词进入英语，成为 register。

items.en: The ending -tio, worn down to -tion, turned the verb of entering into the name of the procedure.
items.cn: 词尾 -tio 磨损为 -tion，把「登记」动词变成这一程序的名称。

items.en: Instruments were said to register a value, and that display became a registration as well.
items.cn: 仪器被说成能 register 一个数值，这一显示也随之被称为 registration。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns of the same record family; the near-meaning group gathers words for enrolling and listing.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「记录」词族的名词；近义组收表示注册与列入的词。

entries.definition: A place where records are kept.
The act of joining a list.
The act of allowing someone to enter.
The act of joining the armed forces.
A written account kept for reference.

normalIntro.en: The noun covers the whole paper trail: the form, the fee, the name, the count, and even the number a dial shows.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词覆盖整条纸面流程：表格、费用、姓名、人数，甚至表盘显示的数字。

normal.en: Register is the act, registration is the whole procedure.
normal.cn: register 是动作，registration 是整个程序。

normal.en: A registration form is the paper you fill before your name counts.
normal.cn: registration form 是名字被算数之前要填的那张纸。

normal.en: A registration fee pays for the record to be kept.
normal.cn: registration fee 是为保存这份记录付的钱。

normal.en: A large registration means many names on the list.
normal.cn: a large registration 指名单上有很多名字。

normal.en: A gauge registration is a record made by a needle instead of a pen.
normal.cn: gauge registration 是针尖而非笔尖做出的记录。

abstract.en: Registration turns a person into a number that a system can hold.
abstract.cn: 登记把一个人变成一个系统能持有的数字。

abstract.en: The deadline is where the paper stops being a possibility.
abstract.cn: 截止日期就是那张纸不再代表可能性的时刻。

abstract.en: Every reading is a registration of something the world just did.
abstract.cn: 每一次读数，都是世界刚刚做了什么的一次登记。

examples.en: Registration closes on Friday at noon.
examples.cn: 报名在周五中午截止。

examples.en: A registration of over three hundred made the hall feel small.
examples.cn: 登记人数超过三百，让这个大厅显得小了。

examples.en: The gauge gave a steady registration of twenty degrees.
examples.cn: 仪表稳定地显示二十度。

dict_mnemonic.text: register（登记）加 ation（名词尾）：登记这件事、被登记的人数、仪表登记下来的读数，都是 registration。

root: 拉丁 gerere（携带）→ regerere（带回、记录）→ regesta（被记下之事）→ registrum（登记簿）→ register ＋ -ation → registration；同族有 register、registrar、registry。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a recorded entry; the senses move from the procedure of recording, to the number recorded, to a reading recorded by an instrument.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被记下的条目」；义项从记录的程序，到被记下的人数，再到仪器记下的读数。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of blank forms and a pen tied by a string at the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：门口长桌上排着一叠待填的表格和一支笔。

branches.en: a form filled at the door
branches.cn: 门口填好的表格

branches.en: three hundred names in a hall
branches.cn: 大厅里的三百个名字

branches.en: a needle resting at twenty
branches.cn: 停在二十的指针

branches.en: forms turned into a total
branches.cn: 表格变成一个总数

branches.en: a number of people and a number on a dial
branches.cn: 人的数目与表盘的数目

intro.en: The verb of entering a record takes the Latin noun ending of action, and the procedure, its total, and its readings all share the name.
intro.cn: 表「登记入册」的动词接上拉丁表行为的名词词尾，程序、总数与读数便共用一个名字。

latinIntro.en: The stem is registrum, a register, with -atio forming the noun of action.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是 registrum（登记簿），-atio 构成表行为的名词。

definition_zh: 规则的；定期的；常规的；常客
definition_en: happening at even intervals; done or happening often; ordinary and usual; a customer who comes often
core_image: 月台上同一时刻出现的那位乘客，手里总拿着同一份报纸
scene: 每天早晨同一时刻，月台上总会出现那位拿着同一份报纸的乘客。He keeps regular hours and rarely works past six.
sceneCN: 这里 regular 是「规律的」（第 1 个义项：间隔均匀、有固定节奏的）；句意为他作息规律，很少工作到六点以后。画面里可留意：同一时刻的月台、同一份报纸。

senses.title: Evenly spaced in time
senses.definition: happening again and again at even intervals
senses.definitionCN: 以均匀的间隔反复发生
senses.example: He keeps regular hours and rarely works past six.
senses.exampleCN: 他作息规律，很少工作到六点以后。
senses.why: The Latin base is a straight rod used for measuring, so regular first means following a straight, even measure.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根是一根用来量度的直尺，所以 regular 首先意为「合乎平直尺度的」。

senses.title: Happening often
senses.definition: done or used frequently as part of a routine
senses.definitionCN: 作为日常惯例而经常进行或使用
senses.example: Regular exercise helped her sleep through the night.
senses.exampleCN: 经常锻炼让她整夜睡得安稳。
senses.why: A thing done at even intervals soon becomes a habit, and the habit is what the word describes.
senses.whyCN: 按均匀间隔去做的事很快成为习惯，而这个词描述的正是这种习惯。

senses.title: Ordinary and usual
senses.definition: normal or standard rather than special
senses.definitionCN: 正常、标准的，而非特殊的
senses.example: The shop was out of the regular size, so she took the large one.
senses.exampleCN: 店里没有常规尺码，她只好拿了大号。
senses.why: What follows the rule is also what is expected, so the word slides from even to ordinary.
senses.whyCN: 合乎规则的东西也是被预期的东西，于是这个词从「均匀」滑向「普通」。

intro.en: Regular comes from a Latin word for a straight measuring rod: to be regular is to follow a line that does not bend.
intro.cn: regular 出自拉丁语中「直的量尺」一词：regular 就是沿着一条不弯的线走。

items.en: Regere meant to rule and to keep straight, the root of a large family about order.
items.cn: regere 意为统治与使直，是有关秩序的大词族的根。

items.en: Regula was a straight stick used to measure or draw a line, and so also a rule.
items.cn: regula 是一根用来量度或画线的直尺，因此也指规则。

items.en: Regularis meant belonging to a rule, and it described things that follow a pattern.
items.cn: regularis 意为「属于规则的」，用来描述合乎某种模式的事物。

items.en: Old French reguler passed the adjective into English with the sense of orderly.
items.cn: 古法语 reguler 把这个形容词带入英语，义为「有秩序的」。

items.en: English widened the word from what follows a rule to what is simply usual and ordinary.
items.cn: 英语把这个词从「合乎规则」扩展到「平常普通」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin regula; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of steady and usual things.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁 regula 构成的词；近义组收表示稳定与平常的形容词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a straight measuring rod: whatever follows its even marks is regular.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一根直的量尺：凡是沿着它均匀刻度走的，就是 regular。

normal.en: Regula is a ruler, so regular means as even as a ruler.
normal.cn: regula 是尺子，所以 regular 意为像尺子一样均匀。

normal.en: Regular intervals are gaps of the same size.
normal.cn: regular intervals 是大小相同的间隔。

normal.en: A regular customer is one who comes again and again.
normal.cn: a regular customer 是反复来的人。

normal.en: Regular size is the ordinary one, not the special one.
normal.cn: regular size 是普通的尺码，不是特制的。

normal.en: Regularly is the adverb: the same thing at the same times.
normal.cn: regularly 是副词：同样的事在同样的时间发生。

abstract.en: A regular life is not a dull one; it is a life with a measure.
abstract.cn: 规律的生活不是乏味的生活，而是有尺度的生活。

abstract.en: What is regular can be trusted, and trust is built on repetition.
abstract.cn: 有规律的可以信赖，而信赖建立在重复之上。

abstract.en: The ordinary is regular by definition, and that is its strength.
abstract.cn: 平常之物按定义就是有规律的，这正是它的力量。

examples.en: He keeps regular hours and rarely works past six.
examples.cn: 他作息规律，很少工作到六点以后。

examples.en: Regular exercise helped her sleep through the night.
examples.cn: 经常锻炼让她整夜睡得安稳。

examples.en: The shop was out of the regular size, so she took the large one.
examples.cn: 店里没有常规尺码，她只好拿了大号。

dict_mnemonic.text: regula（尺子）加 ar：像尺子刻度一样均匀，就是规律；按这个节奏常来常做，就是定期、常规。

root: 拉丁 regere（统治、使直）→ regula（直尺、规则）→ regularis（合乎规则的）→ 古法语 reguler → 英语 regular；同族有 regularly、regularity、regularize，形近的 regulate、regulation 也出自 regula。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an even measure; the senses move from evenly spaced repetition, to frequent habit, to what is ordinary.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「均匀的尺度」；义项从间隔均匀的重复，到经常性的习惯，再到平常普通。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same passenger on the platform at the same hour, holding the same paper.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一时刻出现在月台上、拿着同一份报纸的乘客。

branches.en: hours kept without exception
branches.cn: 从无例外的作息

branches.en: exercise repeated each morning
branches.cn: 每天早晨重复的锻炼

branches.en: a shelf of ordinary sizes
branches.cn: 摆着普通尺码的货架

branches.en: an even interval turned into a habit
branches.cn: 均匀的间隔变成习惯

branches.en: what is often done and what is normally sold
branches.cn: 常做的与常卖的

intro.en: A Latin measuring rod gives a noun of rule and an adjective of conformity, and the adjective passes into English as a word for order.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的量尺给出表「规则」的名词与表「合乎规则」的形容词，后者进入英语成为表秩序的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The base is regula, a straight rod and a rule, with -aris forming the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 regula（直尺、规则），-aris 构成形容词。

definition_en: to control an activity by official rules; to adjust a machine or a process so that it stays steady; to keep a feeling or an amount within limits
core_image: 墙上的恒温器被手指轻轻拧动一格
scene: 墙上的恒温器被手指轻轻拧动一格，暖气随之安静下来。A small device regulates the temperature of the tank.
sceneCN: 这里 regulates 是 regulate 的第三人称单数，取「调节」（第 2 个义项：调整设备使保持稳定）；句意为一个小装置调节着水箱的温度。画面里可留意：被拧动一格的恒温器、安静下来的暖气。

senses.title: To control by rules
senses.definition: to control an activity or a business through official rules
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式规章控制某项活动或行业
senses.example: The agency regulates the sale of medicines.
senses.exampleCN: 这个机构监管药品的销售。
senses.why: The word is built on the Latin word for a rule, so the first sense is simply to apply a rule to something.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建立在拉丁语表「规则」的词上，所以第一义就是把规则施加于某物。

senses.title: To adjust for steadiness
senses.definition: to adjust a machine or a process so that it stays at the right level
senses.definitionCN: 调整机器或过程，使其保持在合适的水平
senses.example: A small device regulates the temperature of the tank.
senses.exampleCN: 一个小装置调节着水箱的温度。
senses.why: A thermostat applies a rule to heat: it measures, compares, and corrects, which is regulation without paper.
senses.whyCN: 恒温器把一条规则用于热量：测量、比较、修正，这是没有纸面的管理。

senses.title: To keep within limits
senses.definition: to hold a feeling, an amount, or a habit within reasonable limits
senses.definitionCN: 把情绪、数量或习惯控制在合理范围内
senses.example: He learned to regulate his temper in front of the class.
senses.exampleCN: 他学会在全班面前控制自己的脾气。
senses.why: Governing a state and governing a temper use the same verb, because both keep something from running past its limit.
senses.whyCN: 治理国家与控制脾气用同一个动词，因为两者都是不让某物越过限度。

intro.en: Regulate is to apply a rule: the Latin noun for a straight rod became a verb of controlling and adjusting.
intro.cn: regulate 就是「施加规则」：拉丁语中表直尺的名词，变成了表控制与调节的动词。

items.en: Regere meant to rule and keep straight, the root of the whole family.
items.cn: regere 意为统治与使直，是整个词族的根。

items.en: Regula was a straight rod for measuring, and so a rule or a standard.
items.cn: regula 是一根用来量度的直尺，因此也指规则或标准。

items.en: Regulare meant to direct by a rule or to set in order.
items.cn: regulare 意为按规则指导或使之有序。

items.en: Regulator named one who sets things in order, and the word passed into technical use.
items.cn: regulator 指使事物有序的人，这个词后来进入技术领域。

items.en: With machines, regulate came to mean keeping a process at a steady level automatically.
items.cn: 到了机器时代，regulate 开始表示自动把某个过程维持在稳定水平。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same rule family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of controlling and adjusting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「规则」词族的词；近义组收表示控制与调整的动词。

entries.definition: A body or device that regulates.
To direct or hold in check.
To change slightly for a better fit.

normalIntro.en: The verb puts a rule to work: on a market, on a machine, or on a temper.
normalIntro.cn: 这个动词让一条规则开始工作：作用于市场、机器，或者脾气。

normal.en: Regula is a rule, and regulate is to make a rule act.
normal.cn: regula 是规则，regulate 就是让规则起作用。

normal.en: A thermostat regulates heat the way a teacher regulates a class.
normal.cn: 恒温器调节热量，就像老师管理班级。

normal.en: Strictly regulated industries answer to a public body.
normal.cn: strictly regulated 的行业要向公共机构负责。

normal.en: To regulate your temper is to keep it inside a line.
normal.cn: regulate your temper 就是把脾气关在一条线内。

normal.en: The noun is regulation, the device a regulator.
normal.cn: 名词是 regulation，装置是 regulator。

abstract.en: To regulate is to decide where the limit lies, and then hold it.
abstract.cn: 调节就是先决定限度在哪里，然后守住它。

abstract.en: A machine that regulates itself is trusted to have no moods.
abstract.cn: 能自我调节的机器被相信是没有情绪的。

abstract.en: Self-regulation is the hardest kind, because no one else holds the rod.
abstract.cn: 自律是最难的一种，因为尺子不在别人手里。

examples.en: A small device regulates the temperature of the tank.
examples.cn: 一个小装置调节着水箱的温度。

examples.en: The agency regulates the sale of medicines.
examples.cn: 这个机构监管药品的销售。

examples.en: He learned to regulate his temper in front of the class.
examples.cn: 他学会在全班面前控制自己的脾气。

dict_mnemonic.text: regula（规则、直尺）加 ate（动词尾）：用规则去管一个行业，用尺子去调一个温度，用尺度去控一份情绪。

root: 拉丁 regere（统治、使直）→ regula（直尺、规则）→ regulare（按规则指导）→ 英语 regulate；同族有 regulation、regulator、regulatory，形近的 regular 也出自 regula。

sensesIntro.en: The core is applying a rule; the senses move from official control, to the automatic adjustment of a machine, to keeping a feeling in bounds.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「施加规则」；义项从官方的管制，到对机器的自动调节，再到把情绪约束在界内。

core.cn: 核心意象：墙上的恒温器被手指轻轻拧动一格。

branches.cn: 被批准销售的许可

branches.en: a tank held at one warmth
branches.cn: 保持同一温度的水箱

branches.en: a pause before an angry answer
branches.cn: 发火之前的一次停顿

branches.en: a rule written and a rule built in
branches.cn: 写在纸上的规则与装进机器里的规则

branches.cn: 被稳住的温度与被压住的脾气

intro.en: The noun of a rule becomes a verb of applying it, and the same verb then governs markets, machines, and moods.
intro.cn: 表规则的名词变成施加规则的动词，同一个动词随后治理市场、机器与情绪。

latinIntro.en: The base is regula, a rule; the verb regulare means to set by rule, and -ate forms the English verb.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 regula（规则）；动词 regulare 意为按规则安排，-ate 构成英语动词。

items.meaning: a rule; the act of regulating

definition_en: an official rule made by an authority; the act of controlling an activity; the automatic adjustment of a body or a machine
core_image: 车间墙上贴满打印的条文，最上面一行被红笔圈住
scene: 车间墙上贴着好几张打印的条文，最上面一行被人用红笔圈了出来。New safety regulations came into force last month.
sceneCN: 这里 regulations 是 regulation 的复数，取「规章」（第 1 个义项：由主管部门制定的正式规则）；句意为新的安全规章上月生效。画面里可留意：贴满墙的条文、被红笔圈住的那一行。

senses.title: An official rule
senses.definition: a rule made by a government or an authority to control how something is done
senses.definitionCN: 政府或主管部门为控制做法而制定的规则
senses.example: New safety regulations came into force last month.
senses.exampleCN: 新的安全规章上月生效。
senses.why: The noun of regulate names the product of ruling: a rule that has been written down and given force.
senses.whyCN: regulate 的名词命名「统治」的产物：一条被写下来并被赋予效力的规则。

senses.title: The act of controlling
senses.definition: the activity of controlling an industry or an activity by rules
senses.definitionCN: 用规则控制某个行业或活动的行为
senses.example: The industry has grown used to close regulation.
senses.exampleCN: 这个行业已渐渐习惯受到严格监管。
senses.why: The same noun names the act and its instrument, as government names both the work and the body that does it.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既指行为也指工具，正如 government 既指治理工作也指治理机构。

senses.title: Automatic adjustment
senses.definition: the way a body or a machine keeps a level steady by itself
senses.definitionCN: 身体或机器自行把某个水平维持稳定的方式
senses.example: The regulation of body temperature matters more in extreme cold.
senses.exampleCN: 在极寒中，体温调节更为重要。
senses.why: No rule is written here, yet the body follows one; the word borrows the language of law for the work of biology.
senses.whyCN: 这里并没有写下任何规则，身体却遵循着一条；这个词借用了法律的语汇来描述生理的工作。

intro.en: Regulation is the noun of regulate: it names a written rule, the work of enforcing rules, and the quiet self-adjustment of a living body.
intro.cn: regulation 是 regulate 的名词：它命名写下的规则、执行规则的工作，以及生命体安静的自我调整。

items.en: Regula was a straight rod and a rule, the standard by which things are set.
items.cn: regula 是直尺与规则，是事物据以被校正的标准。

items.en: Regulare meant to set in order by a rule, and its noun named the act of ordering.
items.cn: regulare 意为按规则使之有序，其名词命名这一整理的行为。

items.en: Late Latin regulatio named a setting in order, used of both conduct and mechanics.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 regulatio 指使之有序，兼用于行为与机械。

items.en: French régulation carried the word into English, where it first meant control by rule.
items.cn: 法语 régulation 把这个词带入英语，最初意为按规则控制。

items.en: Physiologists borrowed the term for the body's keeping of a steady state, and the sense spread to machines.
items.cn: 生理学家借这个词表示身体维持稳定状态，这一意义又扩展到机器。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same rule family; the near-meaning group gathers words for rules and supervision.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「规则」词族的词；近义组收表示规则与监督的词。

entries.definition: A body or device that controls.
A rule enforced by the state.

normalIntro.en: The noun names the rule on the wall, the hand that enforces it, and the body that keeps itself steady without any paper at all.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词指墙上的规则、执行规则的手，以及完全不靠纸面而自行保持稳定的身体。

normal.en: Regulate is the act, regulation is both the rule and the act.
normal.cn: regulate 是动作，regulation 既是规则也是这项管理。

normal.en: Safety regulations are rules written to prevent harm.
normal.cn: safety regulations 是为防止伤害而写下的规则。

normal.en: Government regulation watches over an industry.
normal.cn: government regulation 监管一个行业。

normal.en: The regulation of body temperature happens without a rule book.
normal.cn: 体温调节并不需要一本规则手册。

normal.en: Rules and regulations is a common pairing in official writing.
normal.cn: rules and regulations 是公文中的常见搭配。

abstract.en: A regulation is a society deciding in advance where the line is.
abstract.cn: 规章，就是一个社会事先决定界线在哪里。

abstract.en: Too much regulation can protect a market from its own health.
abstract.cn: 过多的管制，可能让市场失去自身的活力。

abstract.en: The body regulates itself, which is the oldest regulation of all.
abstract.cn: 身体自我调节，这是最古老的一种调节。

examples.en: New safety regulations came into force last month.
examples.cn: 新的安全规章上月生效。

examples.en: The industry has grown used to close regulation.
examples.cn: 这个行业已渐渐习惯受到严格监管。

examples.en: The regulation of body temperature matters more in extreme cold.
examples.cn: 在极寒中，体温调节更为重要。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a rule at work; the senses move from a written rule, to the act of enforcing rules, to a body keeping itself steady.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「正在起作用的规则」；义项从写下的规则，到执行规则的行为，再到身体自行保持稳定。

intro.en: The verb of setting by rule takes the Latin noun ending of action, and the noun covers the rule, the enforcing, and the self-adjustment.
intro.cn: 表「按规则安排」的动词接上拉丁表行为的名词词尾，名词便涵盖规则、执行与自我调节。

latinIntro.en: The base is regula, a rule; regulare is the verb, and -atio forms the noun.

items.meaning: a rule; the act of regulating

definition_zh: 使康复；使恢复功能；改造罪犯使之重返社会；恢复名誉、权利或职位；使建筑物、生态恢复良好状态
definition_en: to restore a person to health, ability or a normal place in society, or to bring something back into good condition
core_image: 康复室里，病人双手扶着平行杠重新学迈步，治疗师在旁护着腰
scene: 事故之后，那名木工半年上不了脚手架，康复中心替他排了一套从抬腿到负重的训练。The clinic designed a slow programme to rehabilitate the injured carpenter.
sceneCN: 这里指「通过训练使伤者重新恢复身体功能」，对应第 2 个义项：借助治疗与反复练习，把失去的动作能力一点点建回来；句意为康复中心为受伤的木工安排了一套循序渐进的训练。画面要点：平行杠、治疗师、重新迈出的第一步。

pos.zh: 使康复；改造；恢复（及物动词，宾语可为人、机构、建筑或生态）

derivatives.zh: 加名词后缀（源自拉丁语，表动作或结果）→ 由「使恢复能力」转为「康复、复权的整个过程」
加形容词后缀（表倾向或功能）→ 由「使恢复」转为「有助于康复的」
加过去分词词尾（转作形容词）→ 由「已使恢复」转为「已康复或已恢复资格的」
由拉丁词干（源自 habilis「能干的」）加动词词尾（源自拉丁语，表「使……」）→ 由「能干」转为「使具备能力、使合用」
habilitate 加名词后缀（表动作或结果）→ 由「使有能力」转为「取得资格的过程」
源自拉丁 habilis「易于掌握的、能干的」加名词后缀（表性质）→ 由「能干」转为「能力」这一性质

senses.title: Back to health: a sick body made well
senses.titleCN: 让病后的身体回到健康
senses.definition: to bring a person back to health after illness or injury through care and treatment
senses.definitionCN: 通过照料与治疗，使人在患病或受伤之后恢复健康
senses.example: The team worked for months to rehabilitate patients after the fire.
senses.exampleCN: 团队工作了数月，帮助火灾后的病人康复。
senses.why: The prefix re- means 'again, back', and the Latin base means 'to make able', so the core is not punishment but the return of a capacity that had been lost.
senses.whyCN: 前缀表示「再、回」，拉丁词干意为「使有能力」，因此这个词的核心不是惩罚，而是让一项失去的能力回来。

senses.title: Retraining a joint or limb: step by step
senses.titleCN: 一点一点练回关节与肢体
senses.definition: to train a specific movement or faculty until it works again
senses.definitionCN: 针对某一动作或机能反复训练，直到它重新正常工作
senses.example: She practised daily to rehabilitate her injured shoulder.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天练习，让受伤的肩膀恢复功能。
senses.why: The capacity is concrete: a shoulder, a knee, a step. The verb then names the slow drill that brings the movement back rather than the abstract idea of health.
senses.whyCN: 这里的能力很具体：一个肩膀、一只膝盖、一步路。动词因此指把这动作练回来的缓慢训练，而不是抽象的健康概念。

senses.title: Reform for society: not merely punish
senses.titleCN: 为重返社会而改造，而非只加惩罚
senses.definition: to prepare a convicted person for ordinary life through education, work and treatment rather than mere punishment
senses.definitionCN: 以教育、劳动与治疗帮助已定罪者过普通生活，而不是只施加惩罚
senses.example: The prison runs classes to rehabilitate young offenders.
senses.exampleCN: 这所监狱开设课程，帮助少年犯改过自新。
senses.why: A person who has lost their place in society is treated like a person who has lost a function: the task is to restore the ability to live among others, not to add pain.
senses.whyCN: 失去社会位置的人，被当作失去一项功能的人来处理：任务是恢复他与别人共同生活的能力，而不是增加痛苦。

senses.title: Rights and name restored: the legal sense
senses.titleCN: 恢复权利与名誉的法律义
senses.definition: to give a person back a former legal standing, office or good name
senses.definitionCN: 把某人原先的法律地位、职位或名誉归还给他
senses.example: The decree rehabilitated the officers who had been dismissed.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法令为那些被免职的军官恢复了名誉。
senses.why: This is the oldest use: re- means back, and the person is returned to a position that had been taken away, so the word speaks of standing rather than of the body.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的用法：前缀意为「回」，人被送回一个曾被剥夺的位置，因此这个词讲的是地位，而不是身体。

senses.title: Bricks made usable: buildings brought back
senses.definition: to repair and upgrade a building, district or facility so that it is usable again
senses.definitionCN: 修缮并提升建筑、街区或设施，使其重新可以使用
senses.example: The city plans to rehabilitate the old dock warehouses.
senses.exampleCN: 市政府计划修缮旧码头的仓库。
senses.why: The object shifts from a body to bricks, but the shape of the act is the same: something fallen into disrepair is made fit for use again.
senses.whyCN: 对象从身体换成了砖块，但动作的形状没变：一样陷入失修的东西被重新弄得合于使用。

senses.title: Land healed: an ecosystem restored
senses.titleCN: 让土地与生态恢复健康
senses.definition: to return damaged land, water or habitat to a healthy working state
senses.definitionCN: 使受损的土地、水体或栖息地回到健康的运转状态
senses.example: Volunteers rehabilitated the strip mine into a wetland.
senses.exampleCN: 志愿者把露天矿坑修复成了湿地。
senses.why: Land, too, can lose its functions; the verb treats soil and water as a system whose capacities must be brought back, just as a body's are.
senses.whyCN: 土地也会失去它的功能；这个动词把土壤与水当作一套必须把能力恢复过来的系统，正如对待身体一样。

senses.title: Back in the post: an official reinstated
senses.titleCN: 让官员回到原来的职位
senses.definition: to restore an official to a post, rank or privilege that had been removed
senses.definitionCN: 使官员回到曾被撤销的职位、军衔或特权
senses.example: The board voted to rehabilitate the suspended director.
senses.exampleCN: 董事会投票决定恢复被停职董事的职位。
senses.why: When the lost thing is a seat at the table, the verb moves from bodily capacity to institutional membership, yet the 'making able again' remains.
senses.whyCN: 当失去的东西是桌边的一个席位，这个词就从身体能力转向制度中的成员资格，但「重新使有能力」这一层仍然在。

senses.title: A good name regained: ideas and works
senses.titleCN: 让作品与观念重获好评
senses.definition: to make a neglected or discredited idea, word or artwork respected again
senses.definitionCN: 使被冷落或已被否定的观念、词语或作品重新受到尊重
senses.example: Later critics rehabilitated the painter's early work.
senses.exampleCN: 后来的评论家为这位画家早期的作品恢复了声誉。
senses.why: Reputation is another capacity that can be lost, and the verb extends to anything whose good name has been taken away, from a person to a painting.
senses.whyCN: 声誉也是一种会失去的能力，这个词于是扩展到任何被夺去好评的东西，从一个人到一幅画都可以。

intro.en: Rehabilitate is not a native English construction: it comes from Medieval Latin rehabilitare, itself re- 'again, back' plus habilitare 'to make able', a verb from habilis 'apt, easily handled'. The same family contains ability and habilitate. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: rehabilitate 不是英语本土构造，而来自中世纪拉丁 rehabilitare：由表示「再、回」的前缀加 habilitare「使有能力」构成，后者又出自 habilis「易于掌握的、能干的」；同一词族还有 ability 与 habilitate。年代均为约数。

items.en: Habilis meant apt, handy or easily handled, an adjective built on habere 'to hold'; the idea was fitness for use.
items.cn: habilis 意为易于掌握的、顺手的、能干的，是由 habere「持有」构成的形容词，核心意思是「合用」。

items.en: Habilitare turned the adjective into a verb meaning to make able or to fit something for a purpose.
items.cn: habilitare 把这个形容词变成动词，意为使有能力，或使某物适合某一用途。

items.en: Re- 'again, back' was added to habilitare, and the compound was used in law and church language for restoring a person to a former right or rank.
items.cn: 表示「再、回」的前缀加在 habilitare 上，这个复合词用于法律与教会语言，指把某人恢复到原有的权利或地位。

items.en: English took the word in the sixteenth century, first in legal and ecclesiastical use for restoring standing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪吸收了这个词，最初用于法律与教会语境，指恢复地位。

items.en: The medical and social senses developed later: restoring a patient's body, then preparing an offender for ordinary life.
items.cn: 医学与社会义后来才发展出来：先指恢复病人的身体，再指为罪犯重返普通生活作准备。

items.en: Contemporary usage extends the verb to buildings, districts, ecosystems and the reputation of ideas or works.
items.cn: 当代用法把这个动词扩展到建筑、街区、生态系统，以及观念或作品的声誉。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin ability stem or merely resembles the word in spelling; the second group offers near alternatives for bringing something back to a good state.
note.cn: 第一组或与本词共享拉丁「能力」词干，或只是拼写相近；第二组是「把某物带回良好状态」的近义替代。

entries.definition: To make someone able or fit; it is the base verb without the 'again' prefix, so it lacks the idea of restoring something already lost.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人有能力或合于用途；这是去掉「再」这一前缀的底层动词，因此不含「把已失去之物恢复过来」的意思。

entries.definition: To make someone weak; it is built on the same Latin ability adjective but through a prefix of removal, so it undoes capacity instead of restoring it.
entries.definitionCN: 使某人衰弱；它由同一个拉丁「能力」形容词经表「去除」的前缀构成，因此是拆掉能力而非恢复能力。

entries.definition: To sum up the main points again; it shares the re- prefix and the -ate ending but comes from Latin caput 'head', so it is merely look-alike, not a relative.
entries.definitionCN: 再次概括要点；它与本词共享「再」这一前缀和动词词尾，但出自拉丁 caput「头」，只是形近，并非同源。

entries.definition: The informal short form of rehabilitation, used chiefly for treatment programmes and centres.
entries.definitionCN: rehabilitation 的口语缩略形式，主要用于治疗项目与康复中心。

entries.definition: To bring something back to a former condition; it is broader and does not specify ability, health or standing.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物带回原先的状态；范围更宽，不特别指明能力、健康或地位。

entries.definition: To put a person back into a post or right; it covers only the institutional sense of the word.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人放回职位或权利之中；只覆盖本词的制度义。

entries.definition: To bring a person back into a group or society; it names the social goal rather than the training that achieves it.
entries.definitionCN: 把某人带回群体或社会之中；它指社会目标，而不是达成目标的训练。

entries.definition: To improve a person or institution by removing faults; for offenders it stresses moral change, while this word stresses restored capacity.
entries.definitionCN: 通过去除毛病来改善人或制度；用于罪犯时强调品德转变，而本词强调能力的恢复。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin ability stem, the real 'again' prefix and real derived words such as ability and habilitate.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁「能力」词干、真实的「再」前缀，以及 ability、habilitate 等真实派生词。

normal.en: Habilis means apt or able, and the English word ability comes from the same Latin adjective.
normal.cn: habilis 意为能干的、合用的，英语 ability 正出自同一个拉丁形容词。

normal.en: The prefix re- means again or back, so the word says the ability is brought back.
normal.cn: 前缀意为「再、回」，所以这个词说的是把能力带回来。

normal.en: Habilitate is the base verb 'to make able'; rehabilitate adds the return to a former state.
normal.cn: habilitate 是底层动词「使有能力」，rehabilitate 则再加「回到原先状态」这一层。

normal.en: Fixed phrases show the range: rehabilitate offenders, rehabilitate a building, drug rehabilitation.
normal.cn: 固定搭配展现范围：改造罪犯、修缮建筑、戒毒康复。

normal.en: The noun rehabilitation and the adjective rehabilitative both keep the idea of making fit again.
normal.cn: 名词 rehabilitation 与形容词 rehabilitative 都保留「重新弄得合用」这一意思。

abstract.en: Picture a patient gripping parallel bars and lifting one foot again.
abstract.cn: 想象病人握住平行杠，再一次把一只脚抬起来。

abstract.en: Picture a released prisoner handed a work badge at a factory gate.
abstract.cn: 想象一名获释的服刑人员在工厂门口接过工牌。

abstract.en: Picture a ruined brick warehouse with fresh scaffolding around it.
abstract.cn: 想象一座破败的砖砌仓库四周搭起了新的脚手架。

examples.en: Therapy helped rehabilitate her knee after the operation.
examples.cn: 治疗帮助她的膝盖在手术后恢复功能。

examples.en: Programmes that rehabilitate offenders cost less than long sentences.
examples.cn: 改造罪犯的项目比长期监禁花费更少。

examples.en: The trust hopes to rehabilitate the discredited theory with new evidence.
examples.cn: 该基金会希望用新证据为这个已被否定的理论恢复声誉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞哈比立忒」——瑞气回来，比着平行杠把腿立起来，人又能站直了 → 康复、复权

root: 拉丁语表「回、再」的前缀 + habilitare「使有能力」（← habilis「易于掌握的、能干的」← habere「持有」）→ 中世纪拉丁 rehabilitare「使恢复能力与资格」；同族词有 ability、habilitate、rehabilitation。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses keep the same movement: something that once had a capacity lost it, and the verb brings that capacity back. The capacity may be health, a movement, a place in society, a legal right, a building's usefulness, a landscape's fertility, a post or a good name.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项守着同一个动作：某样东西本来具有一项能力，后来失去了，这个动词把它带回来。这项能力可以是健康、一个动作、社会位置、法律权利、建筑的可用性、土地的生机、一个职位，或一份好评。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands on parallel bars, one foot lifted again after a long pause.
core.cn: 核心意象：双手扶住平行杠，停歇很久之后那只脚又一次抬起来。

branches.en: THE BODY: health returns first as a general condition, then as a single joint or step trained back into use.
branches.cn: 身体：健康先以整体状态回来，随后又以某个关节或某一步被练回可用。

branches.en: THE PLACE AMONG OTHERS: an offender is fitted for ordinary life, and an official is put back into a lost post.
branches.cn: 人群中的位置：让罪犯重新适合普通生活，也让官员回到失去的职位。

branches.en: THE LEGAL NAME: rights and reputation are handed back by formal decision.
branches.cn: 法律上的名分：权利与名誉经正式决定被归还。

branches.en: THE MADE WORLD: bricks and land are repaired until they can work again.
branches.cn: 人造与自然之物：砖石与土地被修整到能重新运转。

branches.en: THE GOOD NAME OF THINGS: even a discredited idea or artwork can be given its standing back.
branches.cn: 事物的好评：连一个被否定的观念或作品，也能重新得到它应有的地位。

intro.en: Rehabilitate is assembled from Latin pieces: a prefix of return, an adjective stem meaning able, and a verb ending, with English noun and adjective suffixes added later.
intro.cn: rehabilitate 由拉丁成分拼成：一个表示「回、再」的前缀、一个意为「能干」的形容词词干，以及一个动词词尾；英语的名词与形容词后缀是后来才加上去的。

latinIntro.en: Latin habilis 'apt' came from habere 'to hold', and it also produced habilitare, rehabilitare and the English word ability.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 habilis「合用的、能干的」出自 habere「持有」，它还衍生出 habilitare、rehabilitare 以及英语的 ability。

items.meaning: again; back to a former state
items.example: The prefix marks the return of something that was lost.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出「失去之物重新回来」。

items.example: The stem describes a person or thing that can be handled well.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干描述一个人或物能被好好使用。

items.structure: stem of Latin habilitare (to make able)
items.example: The stem carries the act of fitting someone for a task.
items.exampleCN: 这个词干承载「使人适合某项任务」的动作。

items.meaning: to make; to cause to be
items.meaningCN: 使成为；使处于某种状态
items.example: The ending marks the word as a verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个结尾把该词标为动词。

items.example: The clinic aims to rehabilitate each patient.
items.exampleCN: 康复中心的目标是让每位病人恢复功能。

items.example: Rehabilitation takes many months after a severe injury.
items.exampleCN: 重伤之后康复需要许多个月。
该病区提供康复性照护。

items.example: The rehabilitated building reopened as a school.
items.exampleCN: 修缮后的建筑作为学校重新开放。

items.meaning: the process of making someone able
items.exampleCN: 先具备能力，才能独立工作。

items.example: The injury did not damage her ability to walk.
items.exampleCN: 这次受伤没有损害她行走的能力。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 合用的；易于掌握的；能干的

latinEntries.meaning: to restore to a former right or capacity
latinEntries.meaningCN: 恢复原有的权利或能力

definition_en: to make a structure stronger by adding material; to make a feeling, idea, or habit stronger; to send more soldiers to a place
core_image: 墙里露出的钢筋被一层层混凝土包住
scene: 工地上，工人把钢筋编进墙面，再浇上混凝土，墙面一下厚了许多。Steel bars reinforce the concrete floor.
sceneCN: 这里 reinforce 是「加固」（第 1 个义项：通过添加材料使结构更坚固）；句意为钢筋加固了混凝土地面。画面里可留意：编进墙面的钢筋、浇上的混凝土。

senses.title: To make a structure stronger
senses.definition: to add material to a wall, a floor, or a frame so that it can bear more
senses.definitionCN: 给墙、地面或框架添加材料，使其承受更多
senses.example: Steel bars reinforce the concrete floor.
senses.exampleCN: 钢筋加固了混凝土地面。
senses.why: The core of the word is the Latin adjective for strong; the prefix merely adds force to it, so the sense is to put strength in, not to make something strong a second time.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的核心是拉丁语表「强壮」的形容词；前缀只是给它加力，所以意思是「把强度加进去」，而不是「再让它结实一次」。

senses.title: To make an idea stronger
senses.definition: to make a belief, a habit, or an impression firmer
senses.definitionCN: 使信念、习惯或印象更加牢固
senses.example: Every repetition reinforces the habit until it feels natural.
senses.exampleCN: 每一次重复都在强化这个习惯，直到它显得自然。
senses.why: A belief is strengthened the way a wall is: something is added from outside, again and again, until it holds.
senses.whyCN: 信念的加强和墙一样：外来的东西一次次添上，直到它立得住。

senses.title: To send more troops
senses.definition: to add more soldiers or equipment to a force
senses.definitionCN: 为一支部队增加士兵或装备
senses.example: The general reinforced the bridge with two more companies.
senses.exampleCN: 将军又调来两个连增援那座桥。
senses.why: Men and steel are both material added to a position that must hold, so the military sense follows the building sense naturally.
senses.whyCN: 人与钢都是加到「必须守住的位置」上的材料，因此军事义自然地跟着建筑义而来。

intro.en: Reinforce rests on the Latin word for strong, not on a prefix meaning again plus the word force; the prefix strengthens, it does not repeat.
intro.cn: reinforce 立足的拉丁词是「强壮」，而不是「再次」前缀加 force；前缀起加强作用，并不表示重复。

items.en: Fortis meant strong and firm, and it is the true centre of the whole word.
items.cn: fortis 意为强壮、坚固，是整词真正的核心。

items.en: French fort meaning strong descends from fortis, and gives the second half of reinforce.
items.cn: 法语 fort（强壮）出自 fortis，构成 reinforce 的后半部分。

items.en: Enforcier meant to make strong, built with the prefix en- on fort.
items.cn: enforcier 意为使强壮，由前缀 en- 加 fort 构成。

items.en: French renforcer added re- to enforce and meant to strengthen further.
items.cn: 法语 renforcer 在 enforcer 前加 re-，意为进一步加固。

items.en: English took the French word and kept the sense of adding strength, whether to concrete, a belief, or a regiment.
items.cn: 英语接过这个法语词，保留了「添加力量」之义，无论对象是混凝土、信念还是一团兵力。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same root of strength; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of strengthening and supporting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「强壮」词根的词；近义组收表示加强、支持的动词。

entries.definition: To make people obey a rule.
The use of energy to do something.
To hold up or give help to.

normalIntro.en: The word is built on strong: strength is put in from outside, whether as steel, as repetition, or as soldiers.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词建立在「强壮」上：力量从外面加进去，可以是钢筋，可以是重复，也可以是士兵。

normal.en: Fortis means strong, and reinforce means to put strength in.
normal.cn: fortis 意为强壮，reinforce 意为把强度加进去。

normal.en: Rebar reinforces concrete the way a habit reinforces a belief.
normal.cn: 钢筋加固混凝土，习惯强化信念。

normal.en: The prefix re- here adds force; it does not mean once more.
normal.cn: 这里的前缀 re- 是加力，不是「再一次」。

normal.en: Reinforcements are troops sent to hold a line.
normal.cn: reinforcements 是派去守住阵线的部队。

normal.en: Enforce is about rules; reinforce is about strength.
normal.cn: enforce 关乎规则，reinforce 关乎强度。

abstract.en: What is repeated is reinforced, whether or not it deserves to be.
abstract.cn: 被重复的就会被强化，无论它是否值得。

abstract.en: A weak argument repeated only reinforces the doubt.
abstract.cn: 一个薄弱的论点被重复，只会强化怀疑。

abstract.en: Every structure is a promise that it will hold, and reinforcement keeps that promise.
abstract.cn: 每一座结构都是一个「我会撑住」的承诺，加固就是守住这个承诺。

examples.en: Steel bars reinforce the concrete floor.
examples.cn: 钢筋加固了混凝土地面。

examples.en: Every repetition reinforces the habit until it feels natural.
examples.cn: 每一次重复都在强化这个习惯，直到它显得自然。

examples.en: The general reinforced the bridge with two more companies.
examples.cn: 将军又调来两个连增援那座桥。

dict_mnemonic.text: in（向内）加 fort（强壮）加 re 的加力：把强壮塞进去，就是加固；把力量再添一层，就是加强、增援。

root: 拉丁 fortis（强壮）→ 法语 fort（强壮）→ 古法语 enforcier（使强壮）→ 法语 renforcer（进一步加固）→ 英语 reinforce；核心是 in + fortis，不是 re + force。同族有 reinforcement、reinforced、reinforcer。

sensesIntro.en: The core is adding strength; the senses move from material put into a structure, to repetition that firms a belief, to men sent to hold a position.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「添加力量」；义项从加进结构的材料，到使信念牢固的重复，再到派去守阵地的兵力。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: steel bars woven into a wall and buried under fresh concrete.
core.cn: 核心意象：墙里露出的钢筋被一层层混凝土包住。

branches.en: a floor that bears more weight
branches.cn: 承重更大的地面

branches.en: a habit repeated into nature
branches.cn: 重复成自然的习惯

branches.en: two companies sent to a bridge
branches.cn: 派往桥头的两个连

branches.en: steel and soldiers added to a line
branches.cn: 加到一条线上的钢与人

branches.en: repetition that hardens like concrete
branches.cn: 像混凝土一样变硬的重复

intro.en: A Latin adjective of strength becomes a French verb of strengthening, and English adds another layer of force to it.
intro.cn: 拉丁语表「强壮」的形容词变成法语表「使强壮」的动词，英语又在它上面加了一层力。

latinIntro.en: The base is fortis, strong; en- and re- are intensifying prefixes, not a prefix of repetition.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 fortis（强壮）；en- 与 re- 都是加强语气的前缀，不是表重复的前缀。

definition_zh: 加强；增援；强化；（心理学）强化；加固
definition_en: the act of making something stronger, or additional support that strengthens a force, structure or behaviour
core_image: 一面墙外侧被加上斜撑钢架，墙体因此不再晃动
scene: 这里指「加强」。 Positive reinforcement made the pupils keep raising their hands.
sceneCN: 这里 reinforcement 指「行为强化」（第 3 个义项：用奖励提高某种行为出现的频率）；句意：正向强化让学生们持续举手。图中可辨识物件：举手的学生、星星贴纸、行为记录表、教师。

pos.zh: 加强；增援；强化；（心理学）强化；（建筑）加固

senses.title: Making stronger
senses.titleCN: 加强：使原有力量或效果更强
senses.definition: the act of making something stronger or more effective
senses.definitionCN: 使某事物更强或更有效的行动
senses.example: The evidence was a reinforcement of the earlier claim.
senses.exampleCN: 这些证据加强了先前的说法。
senses.why: The noun is re- 'again' + in- 'in' + fortis 'strong' + -ment: literally a making strong again from within.
senses.whyCN: 该名词由 re-「再次」、in-「向内」、fortis「强」与 -ment 构成，字面是「再从内部使强」。

senses.title: Military reinforcement
senses.titleCN: 军事增援：增派兵力或装备
senses.definition: the sending of additional troops or equipment to strengthen a force
senses.definitionCN: 增派部队或装备以加强某支力量
senses.example: Reinforcements arrived before the second assault.
senses.exampleCN: 增援在第二次进攻前抵达。
senses.why: The oldest concrete sense is military: a force is made strong again by adding fresh units.
senses.whyCN: 最早的具体义项是军事：通过加入新生力量，让一支部队重新变强。

senses.title: Positive reinforcement
senses.titleCN: 正向强化：以奖励提高行为频率
senses.definition: in behavioural psychology, the delivery of a reward that increases the likelihood of a behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 行为心理学中给予奖励、从而提高某行为出现概率的做法
senses.example: Positive reinforcement made the pupils keep raising their hands.
senses.exampleCN: 正向强化让学生们持续举手。
senses.why: Behaviourism borrowed the strengthening image: a stimulus follows a behaviour and makes that behaviour more likely to recur.
senses.whyCN: 行为主义借用了「加强」意象：刺激跟在行为之后，使该行为更可能再次出现。

senses.title: Negative reinforcement
senses.titleCN: 负向强化：撤走厌恶刺激来提高行为频率
senses.definition: in behavioural psychology, the removal of an unpleasant stimulus that increases the likelihood of a behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 行为心理学中撤走不愉快刺激、从而提高某行为出现概率的做法
senses.example: Turning off the loud alarm after the correct move was negative reinforcement.
senses.exampleCN: 正确操作后关掉刺耳警报属于负向强化。
senses.why: The label is about removal, not punishment: taking away something unpleasant strengthens the behaviour that made it stop.
senses.whyCN: 这个标签讲的是「撤走」而非惩罚：去掉不快之物，强化了使其中止的行为。

senses.title: Structural reinforcement
senses.titleCN: 结构加固：给建筑补入承载构件
senses.definition: the addition of steel, fibre or other material to make a structure carry more load
senses.definitionCN: 加入钢材、纤维或其他材料，使结构承受更大荷载
senses.example: Steel reinforcement runs through the concrete floor slab.
senses.exampleCN: 钢筋混凝土楼板中布有钢筋。
senses.why: Engineering uses the same logic physically: extra material is put inside so the whole can bear more force.
senses.whyCN: 工程在物理层面沿用同一逻辑：把额外材料放进内部，使整体承受更大力量。

senses.title: Reinforcement learning
senses.titleCN: 强化学习：靠奖励信号调整策略
senses.definition: in machine learning, a method in which an agent improves its decisions from rewards and penalties
senses.definitionCN: 机器学习中智能体依据奖励与惩罚改进决策的方法
senses.example: Reinforcement learning trained the robot to walk on rough ground.
senses.exampleCN: 强化学习训练机器人在地面不平处行走。
senses.why: The algorithm receives a score after each action, so successful actions are reinforced in the policy.
senses.whyCN: 算法在每次行动后得到评分，因此成功的行动在策略中被强化。

senses.title: Social reinforcement
senses.titleCN: 社会性强化：靠赞许与关注维持行为
senses.definition: the strengthening of behaviour through approval, attention or status from other people
senses.definitionCN: 通过他人的赞许、关注或地位来加强行为
senses.example: A nod from the group is powerful social reinforcement.
senses.exampleCN: 群体的一次点头就是有力的社会性强化。
senses.why: Humans add a social layer to the reward model: approval itself can act as the reward.
senses.whyCN: 人类在奖励模型上加了社会一层：赞许本身就能充当奖励。

senses.title: Reinforcing a lesson
senses.titleCN: 巩固：重复与补充使知识更牢
senses.definition: the act of repeating or adding material so that learning or an argument is better retained
senses.definitionCN: 通过重复或补充材料，使学习或论证更牢固的行为
senses.example: The homework is reinforcement of the morning's lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 这份作业是对上午课程的巩固。
senses.why: Education borrows the strengthening metaphor: practice makes a skill hold, as if a wall were buttressed.
senses.whyCN: 教育借用了「加固」隐喻：练习让技能站得住，仿佛给墙加了扶壁。

intro.en: Reinforcement comes from reinforce, which entered English through French renforcer, from re- 'again' and enforcer 'to strengthen', ultimately from Latin fortis 'strong'.
intro.cn: reinforcement 出自 reinforce，后者经法语 renforcer 进入英语，由 re-「再次」与 enforcer「使强」构成，最终源于拉丁 fortis「强壮的」。

items.en: Fortis meant 'strong, powerful'. Its descendants include fort, fortress, effort, comfort and reinforce.
items.cn: fortis 意为「强壮的、有力的」，其后代包括 fort、fortress、effort、comfort、reinforce。

items.en: Old French renforcer meant 'to strengthen, make firm'. The prefix re- has an intensive force here, 'thoroughly', rather than simply 'again'.
items.cn: 古法语 renforcer 意为「加强、使坚固」。此处前缀 re- 带加强语气，意为「彻底」，而不只是「再次」。

items.en: English reinforce appears in the fourteenth and fifteenth centuries, first in military and structural contexts.
items.cn: 英语 reinforce 于 14 至 15 世纪出现，最早用于军事与结构语境。

items.en: Reinforcement adds -ment, the noun suffix from Latin -mentum, naming the act or the added material.
items.cn: reinforcement 加 -ment，即出自拉丁 -mentum 的名词后缀，命名动作或所加材料。

items.en: Twentieth-century behaviourism gave the word its learning sense: a consequence that strengthens a response.
items.cn: 20 世纪行为主义赋予该词学习义：强化某一反应的结果。

items.en: The exact first English date is uncertain, and the relative weight of the French re- as 'again' or as an intensifier is debated.
items.cn: 来源不确定（前缀语义与首见年代）：英语首见确切年代存疑；法语 re- 究竟表「再次」还是加强语气，仍有争论。

note.en: The first group separates the reinforce family; the second gives near-synonyms for strengthening and for reward.
note.cn: 第一组区分 reinforce 词族；第二组给出关于加强和奖励的近义词。

entries.definition: To make stronger or send more support. Reinforcement is the act or the added support.
entries.definitionCN: 指使更强或增派支援；reinforcement 是动作或所加支援。

entries.definition: Describing material or a structure that has been strengthened, such as reinforced concrete.
entries.definitionCN: 形容被加强的材料或结构，如钢筋混凝土。

entries.definition: In psychology, the reward itself; in construction, the strengthening element. It is the thing, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 心理学中指奖励物本身；建筑中指加固件。它是物，不是过程。

entries.definition: Physical power or a body of troops. It lacks the prefix that marks added strength.
entries.definitionCN: 指物理力量或一支部队；缺少表示「额外加强」的前缀。

entries.definition: Any process that makes something stronger. Reinforcement often implies adding something from outside or inside.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指使某物更强的过程；reinforcement 常暗示从外部或内部添加某物。

entries.definition: Bearing weight or giving help. It may be passive, while reinforcement actively adds strength.
entries.definitionCN: 指承重或给予帮助，可以是被动的；reinforcement 则主动增加强度。

entries.definition: Something given for behaviour. In psychology it is the content of positive reinforcement.
entries.definitionCN: 指为某行为给予的东西；心理学中它是正向强化的内容。

entries.definition: Combining parts into a firm whole. It stresses unity, while reinforcement stresses added strength.
entries.definitionCN: 指把部分合成坚固整体，强调统一；reinforcement 强调增加强度。

entries.definition: Extra people or resources held ready. It overlaps military reinforcement but suggests a reserve role.
entries.definitionCN: 指备用的额外人员或资源；与军事增援重叠，但暗示预备角色。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: re- + in- + fortis 'strong' + -ment: strength put back inside.
normal.cn: re- + in- + fortis「强」+ -ment：把强度重新放进内部。

normal.en: The family runs reinforce, reinforced, reinforcer, fort, fortress, effort.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 reinforce、reinforced、reinforcer、fort、fortress、effort。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: positive reinforcement, steel reinforcement, military reinforcement, reinforcement learning.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：正向强化、钢筋加固、军事增援、强化学习。

normal.en: Negative reinforcement removes something unpleasant; punishment adds something unpleasant.
normal.cn: 负向强化撤走不快之物；惩罚则加入不快之物。

normal.en: In concrete, steel reinforcement sits inside the slab and carries tension.
normal.cn: 混凝土中，钢筋位于板内并承受拉力。

abstract.en: Picture a wall leaning outward until a diagonal brace is bolted to its face.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵墙向外倾斜，直到一条斜撑被栓到墙面上。

abstract.en: Picture a star sticker placed on a chart each time a hand goes up.
abstract.cn: 想象每次举手都在图表上贴一颗星。

abstract.en: Picture a player receiving a score after each move and slowly favouring the winning move.
abstract.cn: 想象棋手每走一步都得到评分，慢慢偏爱制胜的那一步。

examples.en: The bridge needed reinforcement after the earthquake.
examples.cn: 地震之后，这座桥需要加固。

examples.en: The teacher used praise as positive reinforcement, not as a bribe.
examples.cn: 老师把表扬当作正向强化，而不是贿赂。

examples.en: The agent learned the maze through reinforcement learning.
examples.cn: 智能体通过强化学习学会了走迷宫。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（再）+ in（进）+ force（力量）」——再往里面加力 → reinforcement 加强、强化

root: 拉丁 fortis「强壮的」→ 古法语 renforcer「加强」→ 英语 reinforce + -ment。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses add strength in different materials: a claim, an army, a behaviour, a habit, a slab, an algorithm, a social group, and a lesson.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项在不同对象上增加强度：主张、军队、行为、习惯、楼板、算法、群体与课程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a diagonal brace bolted to a leaning wall.
core.cn: 核心意象：斜撑被栓到倾斜的墙面上。

branches.en: MORE STRENGTH: an argument or an army is made stronger by addition.
branches.cn: 更强：主张或军队靠添加而变强。

branches.en: BEHAVIOUR: a reward increases a response, or the removal of something unpleasant does.
branches.cn: 行为：奖励提高反应概率，撤走不快之物也能如此。

branches.en: STRUCTURE: steel inside concrete carries the load.
branches.cn: 结构：混凝土中的钢筋承担荷载。

branches.en: MACHINE LEARNING: scores after actions reshape the policy.
branches.cn: 机器学习：行动后的评分重塑策略。

branches.en: PEOPLE AND LESSONS: approval from others, and practice, hold behaviour in place.
branches.cn: 人与课程：他人的赞许与练习把行为固定住。

intro.en: Reinforcement combines a French-derived verb of strengthening with the Latin noun suffix -ment; the base fortis also yields fort and fortress.
intro.cn: reinforcement 把法语来源的「加强」动词与拉丁名词后缀 -ment 结合；词基 fortis 还衍生出 fort 与 fortress。

latinIntro.en: The fortis family includes fort, fortress, effort, comfort, reinforce and fortitude; all centre on strength, either physical or moral.
latinIntro.cn: fortis 词族包括 fort、fortress、effort、comfort、reinforce、fortitude，核心都是力量，或物理或道德。

items.meaning: the act of strengthening; added support
items.example: The wall needs reinforcement before winter.
items.exampleCN: 这堵墙入冬前需要加固。

items.meaning: to make stronger or add support
items.example: The results reinforce our earlier finding.
items.exampleCN: 这些结果强化了我们此前的发现。

items.meaning: the reward or material that strengthens
items.meaningCN: 起强化作用的奖励或材料
items.example: Praise can act as a reinforcer.

items.exampleCN: 这次攀登花了很大力气。

latinEntries.meaning: suffix forming nouns of act or result
latinEntries.meaningCN: 构成动作或结果名词的后缀

definition_en: to refuse to accept an offer, an idea, or a person; to turn down an application officially; to attack a transplanted organ; a thing thrown out as imperfect
core_image: 一份申请被推回桌边，上面盖着红色的退回章
scene: 窗口里的工作人员看了一眼材料，盖章后把它推回桌边。The committee rejected the plan without discussion.
sceneCN: 这里 rejected 是 reject 的过去式，取「否决」（第 2 个义项：正式驳回一项提议）；句意为委员会未经讨论就否决了这个方案。画面里可留意：被推回的材料、红色的退回章。

senses.title: To refuse to accept
senses.definition: to say no to something offered or proposed
senses.definitionCN: 对提供或提议之物说不
senses.example: She rejected the job because it meant moving abroad.
senses.exampleCN: 她拒绝了这份工作，因为那意味着要移居国外。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to throw back: an offer is cast back to the hand that held it out.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「扔回去」：提议被抛回伸出它的那只手。

senses.title: To turn down officially
senses.definition: to refuse an application, a plan, or a proposal through a formal decision
senses.definitionCN: 通过正式决定驳回申请、计划或提案
senses.example: The committee rejected the plan without discussion.
senses.exampleCN: 委员会未经讨论就否决了这个方案。
senses.why: A formal no is still a throwing back, but now the throw is made on behalf of an office and recorded.
senses.whyCN: 正式的「不」仍是扔回去，只是这一扔代表一个机构，并被记录下来。

senses.title: To attack transplanted tissue
senses.definition: of a body, to refuse to accept transplanted tissue and attack it
senses.definitionCN: 指身体不接受移植组织并加以攻击
senses.example: Her body rejected the new kidney within a week.
senses.exampleCN: 她的身体在一周内就排斥了新的肾脏。
senses.why: The body throws back what it does not recognise as its own, which is the same gesture at the scale of cells.
senses.whyCN: 身体把不认作自身的东西扔回去，这是同一动作在细胞尺度上的表现。

intro.en: Reject is a throwing back: the Latin verb joins a prefix of return to the verb to throw.
intro.cn: reject 是「扔回去」：这个拉丁动词把表返回的前缀接在「投掷」动词上。

items.en: Iacere meant to throw or cast, and it underlies many English verbs of sending.
items.cn: iacere 意为投掷或抛出，是许多英语「送出」类动词的基础。

items.en: Reicere joined re-, back, with iacere and meant to throw back or cast off.
items.cn: reicere 由 re-（往回）与 iacere 组成，意为扔回去或抛开。

items.en: The participle reiectus meant thrown back, and it gave the noun and the adjective their shape.
items.cn: 分词 reiectus 意为被扔回的，名词与形容词的形式都由此而来。

items.en: French rejecter meant to refuse or cast aside, and English borrowed it in that sense.
items.cn: 法语 rejecter 意为拒绝或抛开，英语即以此义借入。

items.en: Modern medicine applied the word to a body casting off transplanted tissue.
items.cn: 现代医学把这个词用于身体排除移植组织的现象。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers verbs built on the Latin verb to throw; the near-meaning group gathers words for refusing.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁「投掷」动词构成的动词；近义组收表示拒绝的词。

entries.definition: To decide something is not worth considering.

normalIntro.en: The word is a throw: an offer, a plan, or a piece of tissue is sent back where it came from.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一次投掷：提议、方案或一块组织，被送回它来的地方。

normal.en: Re plus iacere, back plus throw: to throw an offer back.
normal.cn: re 加 iacere，往回加扔：把提议扔回去。

normal.en: A committee rejects a plan with a vote, not a shrug.
normal.cn: 委员会用投票否决方案，而不是耸耸肩。

normal.en: A body rejects a transplant because it reads it as foreign.
normal.cn: 身体排斥移植器官，因为它把那读作异物。

normal.en: Rejection is the noun, and it hurts more than the verb.
normal.cn: rejection 是名词，它比动词更伤人。

normal.en: Do not confuse reject with eject, which throws something out for good.
normal.cn: 别把 reject 与 eject 弄混，后者是把东西彻底抛出。

abstract.en: To reject an idea is not to have heard it.
abstract.cn: 否决一个想法，并不等于听懂了它。

abstract.en: Every rejection is a decision about what a group will not become.
abstract.cn: 每一次拒绝，都是一个群体关于「不成为什么」的决定。

abstract.en: A body that rejects a gift is only protecting its own outline.
abstract.cn: 排斥外来物的身体，只是在守住自己的轮廓。

examples.en: The committee rejected the plan without discussion.
examples.cn: 委员会未经讨论就否决了这个方案。

examples.en: She rejected the job because it meant moving abroad.
examples.cn: 她拒绝了这份工作，因为那意味着要移居国外。

examples.en: Her body rejected the new kidney within a week.
examples.cn: 她的身体在一周内就排斥了新的肾脏。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回）加 ject（扔）：把递来的提议扔回去，是拒绝；把方案扔回去，是否决；把移植物扔回去，是排斥。

root: 拉丁 iacere（投掷）→ reicere（扔回去）→ reiectus（被扔回的）→ 法语 rejecter → 英语 reject；同族有 rejection、rejective，形近的 inject、project、eject 共用 iacere。

sensesIntro.en: The core is throwing back; the senses move from refusing an offer, to an official no, to a body casting off foreign tissue.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「扔回去」；义项从拒绝提议，到正式的否决，再到身体排除外来组织。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an application pushed back across a counter under a red stamp.
core.cn: 核心意象：一份申请被推回桌边，上面盖着红色的退回章。

branches.en: a job offer turned down
branches.cn: 被拒绝的工作机会

branches.en: a plan stopped by a vote
branches.cn: 被投票否决的方案

branches.en: a kidney the body will not keep
branches.cn: 身体不肯留下的肾脏

branches.en: an offer and a plan both sent back
branches.cn: 提议与方案都被送回

branches.en: a committee and a body both saying no
branches.cn: 委员会与身体都在说不

intro.en: A Latin verb of throwing takes a prefix of return, and the compound moves from arrows to offers and finally to cells.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「投掷」动词接上表返回的前缀，这个复合词从箭矢走到提议，最后走到细胞。

latinIntro.en: The base is iacere, to throw; re- means back, and the participle reiectus feeds the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 iacere（投掷）；re- 表「往回」，分词 reiectus 供给名词形式。

definition_en: to show or see a connection between things; to tell a story or an account; to feel that you understand someone
core_image: 两条看似无关的旧照片被并排放在桌上
scene: 桌上并排摆着两张旧照片，拍摄年份相差很远。She could not relate the two events until she saw the dates.
sceneCN: 这里 relate 是「把……联系起来」（第 1 个义项：看出或说明事物之间的关联）；句意为她看到日期之后才把这两件事联系起来。画面里可留意：并排的旧照片、上面的年份。

senses.title: To see a connection
senses.definition: to show or understand how two things are connected
senses.definitionCN: 说明或理解两件事如何关联
senses.example: She could not relate the two events until she saw the dates.
senses.exampleCN: 她看到日期之后才把这两件事联系起来。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to carry back, and a connection is made when one fact is carried back to another and set beside it.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「带回」，而关联正是在把一个事实带回另一个事实、并排放置时形成的。

senses.title: To tell an account
senses.definition: to give an account of events in speech or writing
senses.definitionCN: 用口头或书面叙述事件的经过
senses.example: He related the whole journey as if it had happened to someone else.
senses.exampleCN: 他讲述整段旅程，仿佛那是发生在别人身上的事。
senses.why: Telling is also a carrying back: the events are brought from memory into the present and handed to a listener.
senses.whyCN: 讲述同样是「带回」：事件从记忆被带到现在，交到听者手里。

senses.title: To feel understood
senses.definition: to feel that you share an experience with someone or something
senses.definitionCN: 感到自己与某人或某物有共同的经历
senses.example: Teenagers relate to songs that name exactly what they feel.
senses.exampleCN: 青少年会对那些准确说出他们感受的歌产生共鸣。
senses.why: When a story is carried back into your own life, you relate to it; the connection is now inside you.
senses.whyCN: 当一个故事被带回你自己的生活，你就对它产生共鸣；此时这条联系在你心里。

intro.en: Relate belongs to the Latin verb to carry: the same stem that gives refer and reference also gives relation and relative.
intro.cn: relate 属于拉丁语表「携带」的动词：给出 refer 与 reference 的同一词干，也给出 relation 与 relative。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry or bear, and it underlies a whole family of verbs of transfer.
items.cn: ferre 意为携带或承载，是整族表转移的动词的基础。

items.en: Referre joined re-, back, with ferre and meant to carry back or report.
items.cn: referre 由 re-（往回）与 ferre 组成，意为带回或报告。

items.en: The supine relatus, carried back, supplied the stem rel- to the later verbs and nouns.
items.cn: 动名词形式 relatus（被带回的）为后来的动词与名词提供了 rel- 词干。

items.en: French relater meant to recount or tell, and English took the verb in that sense first.
items.cn: 法语 relater 意为叙述或讲述，英语先以这个意义借入动词。

items.en: The sense of connecting two things grew from the idea of setting one account beside another.
items.cn: 「把两件事联系起来」这一义，由「把一份叙述放在另一份旁边」的观念发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same carrying family; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of connecting and recounting.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「携带」词族的词；近义组收表示联系与叙述的动词。

entries.definition: To carry meaning into another language.
To tell the details of an event.

normalIntro.en: The word carries one thing back to another: two facts side by side, a story to a listener, or a song to your own life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词把一物带回另一物：两个事实并排，一个故事交给听者，或一首歌带回你自己的生活。

normal.en: Re plus late, back plus carried: to carry one thing back to another.
normal.cn: re 加 late（携带）：把一物带回另一物。

normal.en: Relate to a subject means to see yourself in it.
normal.cn: relate to 一个话题，指在其中看到自己。

normal.en: Be related to can mean connected by blood or by cause.
normal.cn: be related to 既可指有血缘，也可指有因果。

normal.en: To relate a story is to tell it from beginning to end.
normal.cn: relate a story 指从头到尾讲述它。

normal.en: Relation, relationship, and relative all come from the same carried stem.
normal.cn: relation、relationship、relative 都出自同一个「携带」词干。

abstract.en: To relate is to refuse to let a fact stand alone.
abstract.cn: 联系，就是不让一个事实孤立地站着。

abstract.en: We relate to stories that carry our own lives back to us.
abstract.cn: 我们与那些把我们自己的生活带回给我们的故事共鸣。

abstract.en: A mind that relates well is a mind with many bridges.
abstract.cn: 善于联系的心，是一座桥很多的城。

examples.en: She could not relate the two events until she saw the dates.
examples.cn: 她看到日期之后才把这两件事联系起来。

examples.en: He related the whole journey as if it had happened to someone else.
examples.cn: 他讲述整段旅程，仿佛那是发生在别人身上的事。

examples.en: Teenagers relate to songs that name exactly what they feel.
examples.cn: 青少年会对那些准确说出他们感受的歌产生共鸣。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回）加 late（带）：把一个事实带回另一个事实，是联系；把经历带回来讲，是讲述；把故事带回自己身上，是共鸣。

root: 拉丁 ferre（携带）→ referre（带回、报告）→ relatus（被带回的）→ 法语 relater（叙述）→ 英语 relate；同族有 relation、relationship、relative、relatively，形近的 refer、reference 也出 ferre。

sensesIntro.en: The core is carrying one thing back to another; the senses move from a link between facts, to a story told, to a story felt as one's own.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把一物带回另一物」；义项从事实之间的关联，到讲出的故事，再到被当作自身经历的故事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two old photographs laid side by side on a table.
core.cn: 核心意象：两条看似无关的旧照片被并排放在桌上。

branches.en: two dates that explain each other
branches.cn: 彼此解释的两个日期

branches.en: a journey told to a listener
branches.cn: 讲给听者的旅程

branches.en: a song that names your feeling
branches.cn: 说出你感受的那首歌

branches.en: facts joined and events recounted
branches.cn: 被连接的事实与被叙述的事件

branches.en: a story heard and a story lived
branches.cn: 听到的故事与亲历的故事

intro.en: The Latin verb of carrying takes a prefix of return, and its stem then grows a family of nouns about connection and kinship.
intro.cn: 拉丁语的「携带」动词接上表返回的前缀，其词干随后长出整族表联系与亲属的名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is ferre, to carry; re- means back, and relatus supplies the stem rel- for relate and relation.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 ferre（携带）；re- 表「往回」，relatus 提供 relate 与 relation 的 rel- 词干。

definition_en: a connection between two or more things; a member of one's family; the way people or countries deal with each other
core_image: 家谱图上两条分支在同一个名字处交汇
scene: 摊开的家谱图上，两条支线在同一个名字处交汇。There is no relation between the two numbers.
sceneCN: 这里 relation 是「关联」（第 1 个义项：事物之间的联系）；句意为这两个数字之间没有关联。画面里可留意：家谱图上交汇的两条支线。

senses.title: A connection between things
senses.definition: the way two or more things are connected or affect each other
senses.definitionCN: 两个或多个事物相互连接或影响的方式
senses.example: There is no relation between the two numbers.
senses.exampleCN: 这两个数字之间没有关联。
senses.why: The noun names what is produced when one thing is carried back to another: a line drawn between them.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词命名「把一物带回另一物」时产生的东西：两者之间画出的一条线。

senses.title: A family member
senses.definition: a person connected to another by blood or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 因血缘或婚姻而与另一人相连的人
senses.example: She is a distant relation of the old painter.
senses.exampleCN: 她是那位老画家的远亲。
senses.why: Kinship is the oldest form of connection, so the word for a link also names the people joined by it.
senses.whyCN: 血缘是最古老的连接形式，因此表「联系」的词也用来指被这条线连起来的人。

senses.title: Official dealings
senses.definition: the way groups or countries deal with one another, usually in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 团体或国家之间往来的方式，通常用复数
senses.example: The two countries restored diplomatic relations after ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 两国在十年之后恢复了外交关系。
senses.why: States also stand in relation to each other, and the plural names the whole web of those dealings.
senses.whyCN: 国家之间也彼此处于关系之中，复数形式便命名这整张往来之网。

intro.en: Relation is the noun of relate, and like refer it comes from the Latin verb of carrying back.
intro.cn: relation 是 relate 的名词，与 refer 一样出自拉丁语表「带回」的动词。

items.en: Referre meant to carry back and to report, built on ferre, to carry.
items.cn: referre 意为带回与报告，由 ferre（携带）构成。

items.en: Relatio named a bringing back, and Latin writers used it for a report to a body and for a logical connection.
items.cn: relatio 指一种带回，拉丁作家用它表示向机构作报告，也表示逻辑上的关联。

items.en: Old French relacion carried the sense of a report and of a connection between things.
items.cn: 古法语 relacion 兼具「报告」与「事物之间关联」两义。

items.en: English extended the noun to people connected by blood, since kinship is a relation in the plainest sense.
items.cn: 英语把这个名词扩展到有血缘的人，因为亲属是最直白的一种关系。

items.en: In the plural, relations came to name the official dealings between states and groups.
items.cn: 在复数形式中，relations 用来指国家与团体之间的正式往来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers nouns of the same carrying family; the near-meaning group gathers words for connection and kinship.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「携带」词族的名词；近义组收表示联系与亲属的词。

normalIntro.en: The noun names the line drawn between two things, the people joined by blood, and the dealings between states.
normalIntro.cn: 这个名词指两物之间画出的那条线、被血缘连起来的人，以及国家之间的往来。

normal.en: Relate is the act, relation is the line it draws.
normal.cn: relate 是动作，relation 是它画出的线。

normal.en: In relation to means with regard to.
normal.cn: in relation to 意为关于、相对于。

normal.en: A close relation is a near relative, not a near idea.
normal.cn: a close relation 指近亲，不是相近的想法。

normal.en: Diplomatic relations are kept in the plural.
normal.cn: diplomatic relations 用复数。

normal.en: Public relations is the work of managing how people see you.
normal.cn: public relations 是管理公众看法的行当。

abstract.en: A relation is not a thing but a line between things.
abstract.cn: 关系不是一个东西，而是东西之间的一条线。

abstract.en: Every relation changes both sides a little.
abstract.cn: 每一种关系都会稍稍改变双方。

abstract.en: To bear no relation to something is to share no line with it.
abstract.cn: 与某物毫无关系，就是与它不共用任何一条线。

examples.en: There is no relation between the two numbers.
examples.cn: 这两个数字之间没有关联。

examples.en: She is a distant relation of the old painter.
examples.cn: 她是那位老画家的远亲。

examples.en: The two countries restored diplomatic relations after ten years.
examples.cn: 两国在十年之后恢复了外交关系。

dict_mnemonic.text: relate（联系）加 ion（名词尾）：被联系起来的这条线是关联，被这条线连起来的人是亲属，国与国之间的线是交往。

root: 拉丁 ferre（携带）→ referre（带回、报告）→ relatus（被带回的）→ 拉丁 relatio（带回、关联）→ 古法语 relacion → 英语 relation；同族有 relate、relationship、relative、relational。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a line drawn by carrying one thing back to another; the senses move from a link between things, to people joined by blood, to dealings between states.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把一物带回另一物所画出的线」；义项从事物之间的联系，到被血缘连起来的人，再到国家之间的往来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two branches of a family tree meeting at one name.
core.cn: 核心意象：家谱图上两条分支在同一个名字处交汇。

branches.en: two figures with no line between
branches.cn: 之间没有线的两个数字

branches.en: a distant cousin at a funeral
branches.cn: 葬礼上的一位远亲

branches.en: two embassies reopened
branches.cn: 重新开馆的两国使馆

branches.en: a line between numbers and a line between people
branches.cn: 数字之间的线与人与人之间的线

branches.en: family ties and state ties
branches.cn: 家族纽带与国家纽带

intro.en: The noun of carrying back takes the Latin ending of action, and the result names both a logical link and a family tie.
intro.cn: 表「带回」的名词接上拉丁表行为的词尾，结果便同时命名逻辑上的关联与家族中的纽带。

latinIntro.en: The base is relatus, carried back, with -io forming the noun relatio.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 relatus（被带回的），-io 构成名词 relatio。

definition_en: the way two people or groups deal with each other over time; a connection between two things; a romantic partnership
core_image: 两把旧椅子被摆得很近，中间的地面已经磨得发亮
scene: 靠窗摆着两把旧椅子，中间那块地板被来回走动磨得发亮。They built a working relationship over ten years.
sceneCN: 这里 relationship 是「关系」（第 1 个义项：人与人之间长期相处的方式）；句意为他们在十年间建立起一种工作关系。画面里可留意：靠得很近的两把椅子、磨亮的地板。

senses.title: A connection between people
senses.definition: the way two people or groups behave toward each other over a period of time
senses.definitionCN: 两个人或群体在一段时间里彼此相处的方式
senses.example: They built a working relationship over ten years.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在十年间建立起一种工作关系。
senses.why: The suffix -ship turns a relation into a continuing state, so the word names something kept up over time rather than a single link.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ship 把 relation 变成一种持续的状态，因此这个词指的是长期维持的东西，而不是一次性的连接。

senses.title: A connection between things
senses.definition: the way two facts, amounts, or ideas are connected
senses.definitionCN: 两个事实、数量或观念相互联系的方式
senses.example: Researchers found a relationship between sleep and memory.
senses.exampleCN: 研究者发现睡眠与记忆之间存在关联。
senses.why: Things, like people, can be set beside each other, and the line between them is also called a relationship.
senses.whyCN: 事物和人一样可以被并置，而它们之间的那条线也叫 relationship。

senses.title: A romantic partnership
senses.definition: a close personal connection in which two people love each other
senses.definitionCN: 两人彼此相爱的一种亲密关系
senses.example: They were in a relationship for three years before they married.
senses.exampleCN: 他们恋爱三年后才结婚。
senses.why: When the personal connection is the closest kind, the general word is used without any further qualifier.
senses.whyCN: 当这种私人联系是最亲密的一种时，这个泛称就不再加任何限定词。

intro.en: Relationship is relation plus the old English suffix of state: a link that is kept going, not a link merely drawn.
intro.cn: relationship 是 relation 加上古英语表状态的后缀：一条被持续维持的线，而不是仅仅画出的线。

items.en: Relatio meant a bringing back and a connection between things.
items.cn: relatio 意为带回，以及事物之间的关联。

items.en: English relation named a connection, a report, and a kinsman.
items.cn: 英语 relation 指关联、报告与亲属。

items.en: The Old English suffix -ship means a state or a condition, as in friendship and hardship.
items.cn: 古英语后缀 -ship 意为状态或境况，如 friendship 与 hardship。

items.en: Putting -ship on relation produced a word for a connection that lasts and is maintained.
items.cn: 把 -ship 加在 relation 上，造出了表示持久且被维系的关系的词。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word became the ordinary term for a couple's partnership.
items.cn: 在二十世纪，这个词成为指伴侣关系的日常说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same connection family; the near-meaning group gathers words for ties and partnerships.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「联系」词族的词；近义组收表示纽带与伴侣关系的词。

entries.definition: A link between things or people.
A strong feeling that ties people.

normalIntro.en: The word is a relation with a duration: something two sides keep up, day after day.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是有时间长度的 relation：双方一天天维持下去的东西。

normal.en: Relation plus ship: a relation that is kept like a ship at sea.
normal.cn: relation 加 ship：像船在海上一样被维持的 relation。

normal.en: A working relationship is built, not found.
normal.cn: a working relationship 是建起来的，不是捡到的。

normal.en: A relationship between figures is a pattern, not a person.
normal.cn: 数字之间的关系是一种模式，不是人。

normal.en: In a relationship means the couple is committed.
normal.cn: in a relationship 指两人已经在交往。

normal.en: The ship in relationship is a suffix of state, not a boat.
normal.cn: relationship 里的 ship 是表状态的后缀，不是船。

abstract.en: A relationship is a bridge that both ends must repair.
abstract.cn: 关系是一座两端都得修桥的桥。

abstract.en: What is not maintained quietly returns to being two strangers.
abstract.cn: 不维系的东西，会悄悄退回成两个陌生人。

abstract.en: The quality of a life is largely the quality of its relationships.
abstract.cn: 生活的质地，很大程度上是关系的质地。

examples.en: They built a working relationship over ten years.
examples.cn: 他们在十年间建立起一种工作关系。

examples.en: Researchers found a relationship between sleep and memory.
examples.cn: 研究者发现睡眠与记忆之间存在关联。

examples.en: They were in a relationship for three years before they married.
examples.cn: 他们恋爱三年后才结婚。

dict_mnemonic.text: relation（关系）加 ship（状态）：不是画一条线，而是长期维持这种状态，就是 relationship。

root: 拉丁 relatio（带回、关联）→ 英语 relation ＋ 古英语后缀 -ship（状态）→ relationship；同族有 relate、relation、relative、related，词干出自拉丁 ferre（携带）。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a link that is kept up; the senses move from a personal connection over time, to a pattern between facts, to a couple's partnership.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被持续维持的线」；义项从长期的人际联系，到事实之间的模式，再到伴侣关系。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two old chairs set close together, the floor between them worn bright.
core.cn: 核心意象：两把旧椅子被摆得很近，中间的地面已经磨得发亮。

branches.en: a decade of working side by side
branches.cn: 十年并肩工作

branches.en: sleep and memory on one chart
branches.cn: 同一张图上的睡眠与记忆

branches.en: three years before a wedding
branches.cn: 婚礼之前的三年

branches.en: a partnership at work and at home
branches.cn: 工作与家庭中的同一种相伴

branches.en: a pattern between facts and a pattern between people
branches.cn: 事实之间的模式与人之间的模式

intro.en: The noun of connection takes the old English suffix of state, and the compound names a link that continues through time.
intro.cn: 表联系的名词接上古英语表状态的后缀，合成词便命名一条延续于时间中的线。

latinIntro.en: The stem is relatio, a bringing back and a connection; -ship is the English suffix of state.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是 relatio（带回、关联）；-ship 是英语表状态的后缀。

definition_en: true only when compared with something else; connected with a particular subject; a member of one's family
core_image: 两个人站在不同高度的台阶上比身高
scene: 两个人站在不同高度的台阶上，看起来竟一样高。Happiness is relative to what a person expects.
sceneCN: 这里 relative 是「相对的」（第 1 个义项：只有在比较中才成立）；句意为幸福相对于一个人的期待而言。画面里可留意：不同高度的台阶、看起来一样高的两人。

senses.title: True only by comparison
senses.definition: not absolute, but true when measured against something else
senses.definitionCN: 非绝对的，只有在与其他事物比较时才成立
senses.example: Happiness is relative to what a person expects.
senses.exampleCN: 幸福相对于一个人的期待而言。
senses.why: The Latin participle means carried back, and a value carried back to another value is measured by it rather than in itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁分词意为「被带回的」，一个数值被带回另一个数值那里，就是以它为准来衡量，而不是就自身而言。

senses.title: Connected with a subject
senses.definition: having a connection with a particular matter
senses.definitionCN: 与某个特定事项有关联
senses.example: The report gathers the facts relative to the accident.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告汇集了与那场事故相关的事实。
senses.why: Something carried back to a question is relevant to it, and the same adjective names that connection.
senses.whyCN: 被带回到某个问题那里的东西就与它有关，同一个形容词命名这种关联。

senses.title: A family member
senses.definition: a person connected to another by blood or marriage
senses.definitionCN: 因血缘或婚姻而与另一人相连的人
senses.example: A distant relative left her the old house.
senses.exampleCN: 一位远亲把那座老房子留给了她。
senses.why: Persons related by blood are quite literally carried back to a common ancestor, and the adjective became a noun for them.
senses.whyCN: 有血缘的人确实可以被带回同一个祖先，于是这个形容词就成了指他们的名词。

intro.en: Relative is the adjective of the Latin participle carried back; what is carried back is measured against something else, or joined to a family.
intro.cn: relative 是拉丁分词「被带回的」所对应的形容词；被带回的东西，要么以别物为尺，要么归入一个家族。

items.en: Ferre meant to carry, the root of referre and of the whole rel- family.
items.cn: ferre 意为携带，是 referre 与整个 rel- 词族的根。

items.en: Relatus, the participle of referre, meant carried back or having reference to.
items.cn: relatus 是 referre 的分词，意为被带回的或有所指的。

items.en: Relativus meant having relation to something else, the grammatical and philosophical term.
items.cn: relativus 意为与其他事物有关的，是语法与哲学术语。

items.en: English used the adjective for values that hold only in comparison, as opposed to absolute ones.
items.cn: 英语用这个形容词表示只在比较中成立的数值，与「绝对」相对。
