items.en: The noun use for a family member grew from the sense of persons referred to one another by blood.
items.cn: 指亲属的名词用法，由「因血缘而彼此相关的人」这一意义发展而来。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same carrying stem; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of comparison and kinship words.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「携带」词干的词；近义组收表比较的形容词与亲属词。

entries.definition: Changing in step with something else.

normalIntro.en: The word means carried back to something else: a value to another value, a fact to a question, a person to a family.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词意为「被带回别处」：数值带回另一数值，事实带回一个问题，人带回一个家族。

normal.en: Relative to means measured against.
normal.cn: relative to 意为以……为参照来衡量。

normal.en: Relative humidity compares moisture with the maximum the air can hold.
normal.cn: relative humidity 把湿度与空气能容纳的最大量相比。

normal.en: A close relative is a near member of the family.
normal.cn: a close relative 是家族中的近亲。

normal.en: Relative importance ranks things against each other.
normal.cn: relative importance 是把事物相互比较后的轻重。

normal.en: Relative and absolute are a pair; one needs the other.
normal.cn: relative 与 absolute 是一对，彼此需要。

abstract.en: Almost everything we call large is only relatively large.
abstract.cn: 我们所说的大，几乎都只是相对地大。

abstract.en: To see things as relative is not to see them as unreal.
abstract.cn: 把事物看作相对的，并不等于把它们看作虚幻的。

abstract.en: A family is the first place where a person is a relative.
abstract.cn: 家庭是一个人最初成为「亲属」的地方。

examples.en: Happiness is relative to what a person expects.
examples.cn: 幸福相对于一个人的期待而言。

examples.en: The report gathers the facts relative to the accident.
examples.cn: 这份报告汇集了与那场事故相关的事实。

examples.en: A distant relative left her the old house.
examples.cn: 一位远亲把那座老房子留给了她。

dict_mnemonic.text: relate（带回、关联）加 ive：必须带回别物才有意义，是相对；与某个问题带回一处，是相关；因血缘被带回一家，是亲戚。

root: 拉丁 ferre（携带）→ referre（带回）→ relatus（被带回的）→ 拉丁 relativus（有关的）→ 英语 relative；同族有 relatively、relativity、relation、relate。

sensesIntro.en: The core is carried back to something else; the senses move from a value measured by comparison, to a fact tied to a subject, to a person tied to a family.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「被带回别物那里」；义项从以比较为准的数值，到与某个主题相连的事实，再到与家族相连的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people on steps of different heights, looking the same size.
core.cn: 核心意象：两个人站在不同高度的台阶上比身高。

branches.en: two figures that only make sense together
branches.cn: 只有放在一起才有意义的两个数字

branches.en: facts gathered around one accident
branches.cn: 围绕一场事故汇集的材料

branches.en: an old house left by a cousin
branches.cn: 一位远亲留下的老房子

branches.en: a comparison and a reference to a subject
branches.cn: 一次比较与一次对主题的指向

branches.en: tied to a question and tied to a family
branches.cn: 与一个问题相连，与一个家族相连

intro.en: The participle carried back becomes an adjective of comparison, and the adjective then becomes a noun for a family member.
intro.cn: 「被带回的」分词变成表比较的形容词，这个形容词又变成指亲属的名词。

latinIntro.en: The base is relatus, carried back; -ivus forms the adjective relativus.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 relatus（被带回的）；-ivus 构成形容词 relativus。

definition_en: when compared with other things of the same kind; to a fairly great degree, though not absolutely
core_image: 两只手把同一块石头举到不同高度的背景前比较大小
scene: 同一块石头，放在不同高度的背景前，看上去大小完全不同。The room was relatively cheap for the city centre.
sceneCN: 这里 relatively 是「相对地」（第 1 个义项：与同类事物相比而言）；句意为对市中心来说，这个房间相对便宜。画面里可留意：同一块石头在不同背景下的观感。

senses.title: By comparison
senses.definition: when measured against other things of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 与同类事物相比较而言
senses.example: The room was relatively cheap for the city centre.
senses.exampleCN: 对市中心来说，这个房间相对便宜。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the comparison inside the sentence: cheap compared with other rooms, not cheap in itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把比较留在句子内部：与别的房间相比便宜，而不是本身就便宜。

senses.title: Fairly, though not absolutely
senses.definition: to a fairly high degree, with the comparison left understood
senses.definitionCN: 达到相当高的程度，而比较对象被省略
senses.example: The work was finished relatively quickly.
senses.exampleCN: 这项工作完成得相当快。
senses.why: When the other term of the comparison is obvious, the word drifts toward a soft form of very.
senses.whyCN: 当比较的另一方显而易见时，这个词就漂向一种柔和的「很」。

intro.en: Relatively is the adverb of relative, and it keeps the comparison that the adjective implies.
intro.cn: relatively 是 relative 的副词，它保留了形容词所暗示的比较。

items.en: Relatus meant carried back, and what is carried back is always measured against something.
items.cn: relatus 意为被带回的，而被带回之物总是以某物为尺。

items.en: Relativus meant having relation to something else.
items.cn: relativus 意为与其他事物有关的。

items.en: English relative described values that hold only in comparison.
items.cn: 英语 relative 描述只在比较中成立的数值。

items.en: The adverb ending -ly turned the comparison into a way of qualifying a statement.
items.cn: 副词词尾 -ly 把这种比较变成限定陈述的方式。

items.en: Modern speech uses the adverb to soften a claim that would be too strong if stated flatly.
items.cn: 现代口语用这个副词来缓冲一个说得太满的论断。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same comparison family; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of degree and comparison.
note.cn: 形近组收同一比较词族的词；近义组收表程度与比较的副词。

normalIntro.en: The adverb warns the reader that a comparison is being made, even when the other side of it stays silent.
normalIntro.cn: 这个副词提醒读者：这里正在做比较，即使比较的另一方没有说出口。

normal.en: Relatively cheap means cheap next to the other ones.
normal.cn: relatively cheap 指与别的相比便宜。

normal.en: Relatively speaking is the phrase that makes the comparison explicit.
normal.cn: relatively speaking 是把比较说清楚的那个短语。

normal.en: Relatively few means fewer than you might expect here.
normal.cn: relatively few 指比你在这种情况下预期的要少。

normal.en: The word softens a claim without withdrawing it.
normal.cn: 这个词软化论断，但不撤回论断。

normal.en: Drop the comparison and the sentence may become false.
normal.cn: 去掉比较，这句话可能就不成立了。

abstract.en: Every relative judgement borrows its scale from somewhere.
abstract.cn: 每一个相对判断都从某处借来它的尺度。

abstract.en: Relatively is a small word that keeps us honest about context.
abstract.cn: relatively 这个小词让我们对语境保持诚实。

abstract.en: What is relatively safe may still be unsafe enough.
abstract.cn: 相对安全的东西，也可能仍然足够危险。

examples.en: The room was relatively cheap for the city centre.
examples.cn: 对市中心来说，这个房间相对便宜。

examples.en: The work was finished relatively quickly.
examples.cn: 这项工作完成得相当快。

examples.en: Relatively few students chose the harder course.
examples.cn: 相对较少的学生选了那门更难的课。

dict_mnemonic.text: relative（相对的）加 ly：把「跟谁比」这句话塞进一个副词里，就是「相对地」；比较对象省略时，就成了「相当」。

root: 拉丁 relatus（被带回的）→ relativus（有关的）→ 英语 relative ＋ -ly → relatively；与 relative、relativity、relation 同源。

sensesIntro.en: The core is an implied comparison; the senses move from a comparison that is stated, to a softened degree word when the comparison is understood.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「隐含的比较」；义项从明说的比较，到比较对象被省略时的缓和程度词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one stone shown against backgrounds of different heights, seeming to change size.
core.cn: 核心意象：两只手把同一块石头举到不同背景前比较大小。

branches.en: a rent that is low for the area
branches.cn: 在这个地段算低的房租

branches.en: work done faster than expected
branches.cn: 比预期完成得更快的工作

branches.en: a comparison made and a degree implied
branches.cn: 明做的比较与暗示的程度

branches.en: a claim that stops short of very
branches.cn: 没有说到「很」的论断

branches.en: a price judged only against neighbours
branches.cn: 只与邻近房源比较的价格

intro.en: The adjective of comparison takes the English adverb ending, and the result marks a judgement that depends on a scale.
intro.cn: 表比较的形容词接上英语副词词尾，结果便标记一个依赖尺度的判断。

latinIntro.en: The stem is relativus, having relation to; -ly is the English adverb ending.
latinIntro.cn: 词干是 relativus（与其他事物有关的）；-ly 是英语副词词尾。

definition_en: to become less tense in body or mind; to make a rule or a limit less strict; to become less tight or less severe
core_image: 一直攥紧的拳头在长椅上慢慢松开
scene: 他在长椅上坐了很久，一直攥紧的拳头才慢慢松开。A hot bath helps her relax after a long shift.
sceneCN: 这里 relax 是「放松」（第 1 个义项：身体或心情由紧张转为松弛）；句意为长时间轮班之后，热水澡能帮她放松。画面里可留意：慢慢松开的拳头、长椅。

senses.title: To become less tense
senses.definition: to let the body or the mind become loose and calm
senses.definitionCN: 让身体或心情变得松弛平静
senses.example: A hot bath helps her relax after a long shift.
senses.exampleCN: 长时间轮班之后，热水澡能帮她放松。
senses.why: The Latin verb means to loosen, and the prefix adds a returning: tension that has tightened is let back to its resting state.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁动词意为「使松」，前缀则添上「回」的意味：绷紧的张力被放回到休息状态。

senses.title: To make a rule less strict
senses.definition: to make a rule, a limit, or a control less severe
senses.definitionCN: 使规则、限制或管制不那么严格
senses.example: The city relaxed the rules on street markets last spring.
senses.exampleCN: 这座城市去年春天放宽了街头集市的规定。
senses.why: A rule can be tight like a muscle, and loosening it is described with the same verb.
senses.whyCN: 规则可以像肌肉一样紧绷，而松开它用的是同一个动词。

senses.title: To become less tight
senses.definition: to become less firm, less intense, or less severe
senses.definitionCN: 变得不那么紧、不那么强烈或不那么严重
senses.example: His grip on the rail relaxed once the ship was steady.
senses.exampleCN: 船稳下来之后，他抓着栏杆的手松了。
senses.why: Here the loosening is physical again, but the object is a hold or a tension rather than a person.
senses.whyCN: 这里的松弛又回到物理层面，只是对象是握力或张力，而不是一个人。

intro.en: Relax is to loosen: the Latin adjective for loose becomes a verb, and the prefix sets the loosening in motion.
intro.cn: relax 意为「使松」：拉丁语表「松」的形容词变成动词，前缀让这一松开得以进行。

items.en: Laxus meant loose, slack, or wide, and it is the root of the whole family.
items.cn: laxus 意为松的、松弛的或宽的，是整个词族的根。

items.en: Laxare meant to loosen, slacken, or let go.
items.cn: laxare 意为放松、使松弛或放开。

items.en: Relaxare added re- and meant to loosen back, to unbend, or to relieve.
items.cn: relaxare 加上 re-，意为松回去、舒展或缓解。

items.en: French relaxer carried the medical sense of easing tension into English.
items.cn: 法语 relaxer 把「缓解紧张」这一医学用法带入英语。

items.en: English widened the verb from muscles and minds to rules, prices, and controls.
items.cn: 英语把这个动词从肌肉与心情扩展到规则、价格与管制。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on the Latin adjective for loose; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of resting and easing.
note.cn: 形近组收由拉丁语表「松」的形容词构成的词；近义组收表示休息与缓解的动词。

entries.definition: To make less severe or painful.
To relax after work or stress.

normalIntro.en: The word is loosen plus back: a muscle, a rule, or a grip is allowed to return to slack.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「松开加回来」：肌肉、规则或握力被允许回到松弛。

normal.en: Laxus means loose, and relax means to make loose again.
normal.cn: laxus 意为松，relax 意为重新放松。

normal.en: Relax the rules means let them be less strict.
normal.cn: relax the rules 指让规定不那么严。

normal.en: A relaxed person is one whose shoulders have come down.
normal.cn: a relaxed person 就是肩膀放下来的人。

normal.en: The adjective relaxing describes what does the loosening.
normal.cn: 形容词 relaxing 描述起松弛作用的东西。

normal.en: Release and relax are different words; one lets go, one slackens.
normal.cn: release 与 relax 是两个词：一个放开，一个松弛。

abstract.en: To relax is to stop holding what no longer needs holding.
abstract.cn: 放松，就是停止握住已经不必握住的东西。

abstract.en: A mind that never slackens cannot tell what matters.
abstract.cn: 从不松弛的心，分不清什么要紧。

abstract.en: Some rules deserve to be loosened, and some only appear to.
abstract.cn: 有些规则值得放宽，有些只是看起来如此。

examples.en: A hot bath helps her relax after a long shift.
examples.cn: 长时间轮班之后，热水澡能帮她放松。

examples.en: The city relaxed the rules on street markets last spring.
examples.cn: 这座城市去年春天放宽了街头集市的规定。

examples.en: His grip on the rail relaxed once the ship was steady.
examples.cn: 船稳下来之后，他抓着栏杆的手松了。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回）加 lax（松）：把紧绷的肌肉放回松弛，是放松；把绷紧的规定放回松弛，是放宽。

root: 拉丁 laxus（松的）→ laxare（使松）→ relaxare（松回去、缓解）→ 法语 relaxer → 英语 relax；同族有 relaxation、relaxed、relaxing，形近的 lax 也出自 laxus。

sensesIntro.en: The core is slackening; the senses move from a tense body, to a strict rule, to a tight hold.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「变松」；义项从紧绷的身体，到严格的规定，再到握紧的手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fist that has been clenched for hours slowly opening on a bench.
core.cn: 核心意象：一直攥紧的拳头在长椅上慢慢松开。

branches.en: a bath after a long shift
branches.cn: 长班之后的一次泡澡

branches.en: a market rule made easier
branches.cn: 被放宽的集市规定

branches.en: a hand letting go of a rail
branches.cn: 松开栏杆的手

branches.en: a body and a grip both loosening
branches.cn: 身体与握力同时松开

branches.en: a rule and a mind both eased
branches.cn: 被放宽的规定与松弛下来的心

intro.en: The Latin adjective for loose becomes a verb of loosening, and the prefix turns the action into a return to slack.
intro.cn: 拉丁语表「松」的形容词变成表「使松」的动词，前缀把这一动作变成「松回去」。

latinIntro.en: The base is laxus, loose; laxare means to loosen, and re- means back.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 laxus（松的）；laxare 意为使松，re- 表「往回」。

definition_en: to let a person or a thing go free; to make a film, a record, or a report available to the public; to free someone from a duty or a debt
core_image: 笼门被拉开，一只鸟迟疑了一下才飞出去
scene: 笼门被拉开，里面的鸟迟疑了一下，才振翅飞向树梢。The government will release the report on Monday.
sceneCN: 这里 release 是「发布」（第 2 个义项：把消息或文件公开给公众）；句意为政府将在周一发布这份报告。画面里可留意：被拉开的笼门、飞向树梢的鸟。

senses.title: To let go free
senses.definition: to stop holding a person or an animal and let it go
senses.definitionCN: 不再抓住某人或某动物，任其离开
senses.example: The keeper released the bird at the edge of the wood.
senses.exampleCN: 管理员在林边放飞了那只鸟。
senses.why: The French word behind it means to let go or give back, so the first sense is simply the opening of a hand or a door.
senses.whyCN: 其背后的法语词意为「放开、交还」，所以第一义就是把手或门打开。

senses.title: To make public
senses.definition: to make a film, a record, or a piece of information available to everyone
senses.definitionCN: 让影片、唱片或信息向所有人公开
senses.example: The government will release the report on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 政府将在周一发布这份报告。
senses.why: A work kept from the public is held tight; making it available is the same letting go, applied to information.
senses.whyCN: 被扣住不公开的作品是攥紧的；让它面世就是同一种「放开」，只是对象变成了信息。

senses.title: To free from an obligation
senses.definition: to free someone from a duty, a debt, or a promise
senses.definitionCN: 使某人免于某项义务、债务或承诺
senses.example: The court released him from the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 法院解除了他在这份合同中的义务。
senses.why: To be bound by a duty is to be held, and to be released is to have that hold removed.
senses.whyCN: 被义务束缚就是被抓住，而被解除就是那只手被移开。

intro.en: Release came into English through a French verb meaning to let go or give back; in English it is a separate word from relax, which was borrowed straight from Latin.
intro.cn: release 经由一个意为「放开、交还」的法语动词进入英语；在英语里它与 relax 是两个词，后者直接借自拉丁语。

items.en: Old French laissier meant to let, leave, or let go, and it stands behind the second half of the word.
items.cn: 古法语 laissier 意为让、留下或放开，构成这个词的后半部分。

items.en: Relesser joined re- with laissier and meant to let go, give back, or remit.
items.cn: relesser 由 re- 与 laissier 组合，意为放开、交还或免除。

items.en: The French noun reles named a letting go, a remission of a debt, or a release from custody.
items.cn: 法语名词 reles 指放开、债务的免除或从拘押中释放。

items.en: English borrowed both the verb and the noun, keeping the senses of freeing and remitting.
items.cn: 英语同时借入动词与名词，保留了「释放」与「免除」两义。

items.en: Publishing gave the word its sense of issuing a film, a record, or a statement to the public.
items.cn: 出版业赋予这个词「向公众发行影片、唱片或声明」的意义。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that begin like release; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of freeing and issuing.
note.cn: 形近组收与 release 开头相近的词；近义组收表示释放与发行的动词。

entries.definition: The easing of pain or worry.
To let a person or a substance go out.
To make a work available to the public.

normalIntro.en: The word is a letting go: a hand opens, a film reaches the public, a duty falls away.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「松手」：手打开，影片抵达公众，义务随之脱落。

normal.en: Re plus lease, back plus let: to let something go back to freedom.
normal.cn: re 加 lease，往回加让：让某物回到自由。

normal.en: Press release is a sheet handed to journalists.
normal.cn: press release 是发给记者的那张纸。

normal.en: A film release is the day the public may see it.
normal.cn: a film release 是公众可以看到它的日子。

normal.en: Release a prisoner is the plainest use of the word.
normal.cn: release a prisoner 是这个词最朴素的用法。

normal.en: Release and relax are separate words in English; keep them apart.
normal.cn: release 与 relax 在英语里是两个词，要分清。

abstract.en: To release is to admit that holding on has stopped helping.
abstract.cn: 释放，就是承认攥着已经不再有用。

abstract.en: A government releases only what it can no longer hide.
abstract.cn: 政府只发布它再也藏不住的东西。

abstract.en: What is released does not always choose where it goes.
abstract.cn: 被放出的东西，并不总能选择去向。

examples.en: The government will release the report on Monday.
examples.cn: 政府将在周一发布这份报告。

examples.en: The keeper released the bird at the edge of the wood.
examples.cn: 管理员在林边放飞了那只鸟。

examples.en: The court released him from the contract.
examples.cn: 法院解除了他在这份合同中的义务。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回、放开）加 lease（让）：松开手让出去，是释放；把影片或消息让给公众，是发布；把义务让掉，是解除。

root: 古法语 laissier（让、放开）→ relesser（放开、交还、免除）→ 名词 reles → 英语 release；与直接借自拉丁 relaxare 的 relax 是两个分别进入英语的词，不可互训。同族有 releaser、releasable。

sensesIntro.en: The core is letting go; the senses move from opening a cage, to issuing a work to the public, to removing a duty.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「放开」；义项从打开笼子，到向公众发行作品，再到解除一项义务。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cage door pulled open and a bird hesitating before it flies.
core.cn: 核心意象：笼门被拉开，一只鸟迟疑了一下才飞出去。

branches.en: a bird leaving its cage
branches.cn: 离开笼子的鸟

branches.en: a report handed to the press
branches.cn: 交给媒体的报告

branches.en: a contract no longer binding
branches.cn: 不再有约束力的合同

branches.en: a body freed and an obligation lifted
branches.cn: 被放开的人与被卸下的义务

branches.en: a statement issued and a debt forgiven
branches.cn: 发布的声明与免除的债务

intro.en: A French verb of letting go enters English with its noun, and the single idea of releasing covers prisoners, films, and debts.
intro.cn: 一个法语表「放开」的动词连同其名词进入英语，而「放开」这一个观念覆盖囚犯、影片与债务。

latinIntro.en: The stem is French, from laissier, to let; the prefix re- means back, so no Latin root is listed for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自法语 laissier（让），前缀 re- 表「往回」，因此本词不列拉丁词根。

definition_en: closely connected with the subject being discussed; useful and important for a particular purpose
core_image: 一叠材料里只有几页被抽出来放到桌子中央
scene: 一叠厚厚的材料摊在桌上，他从中抽出几页，放到桌子中央。Only the facts relevant to the case were read aloud.
sceneCN: 这里 relevant 是「相关的」（第 1 个义项：与正在讨论的问题直接有关）；句意为只有与本案相关的事实被朗读出来。画面里可留意：被抽出的几页、桌子中央。

senses.title: Connected with the matter
senses.definition: directly connected with the subject or the problem at hand
senses.definitionCN: 与手头的话题或问题直接相连
senses.example: Only the facts relevant to the case were read aloud.
senses.exampleCN: 只有与本案相关的事实被朗读出来。
senses.why: The word began as a picture of something lifted up to help, and it now names whatever lifts a discussion forward.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初描绘被举起以提供帮助之物，如今命名一切能推动讨论向前的东西。

senses.title: Useful and to the point
senses.definition: important and useful for the purpose being considered
senses.definitionCN: 对正在考虑的目的而言重要且有用
senses.example: Her question was short but highly relevant to the decision.
senses.exampleCN: 她的问题很短，却与这项决定高度相关。
senses.why: Connection alone is not enough; the thing must also carry weight, which is why relevant often implies useful.
senses.whyCN: 仅有联系还不够，那件事物还必须具有分量，因此 relevant 常隐含「有用」。

intro.en: Relevant comes from a Latin verb meaning to lift up and relieve, not from the carrying verb behind relate; the two families are distinct.
intro.cn: relevant 出自一个意为「举起、减轻」的拉丁动词，而不是 relate 所属的那个「携带」动词；这两个词族彼此不同。

items.en: Levare meant to lift up or make light, built on levis, light in weight.
items.cn: levare 意为举起或使轻，由 levis（轻的）构成。

items.en: Relevare joined re- with levare and meant to raise up, relieve, or assist.
items.cn: relevare 由 re- 与 levare 组合，意为举起、减轻或援助。

items.en: The participle relevans, lifting up or helping, named what comes to the aid of a matter.
items.cn: 分词 relevans（举起或帮助）指对某件事物施以援手者。

items.en: French relevant meant depending upon or pertinent, and English took the adjective in that sense.
items.cn: 法语 relevant 意为「取决于」或「切题」，英语即以这个意义借入形容词。

items.en: English narrowed the word to what bears on the question under discussion.
items.cn: 英语把这个词收窄为「与正在讨论的问题有关」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words that resemble relevant; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of pertinence.
note.cn: 形近组收与 relevant 形近的词；近义组收表示切题的形容词。

entries.definition: Able to be applied to a case.

normalIntro.en: The word points to what is lifted up to help the discussion: not everything connected, only what carries weight.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词指向被举起来帮助讨论的东西：不是所有有关联的，而是有分量的那些。

normal.en: Relevant to means it bears on the question.
normal.cn: relevant to 指它压在正在讨论的问题上。

normal.en: Relevant experience is experience that helps this job.
normal.cn: relevant experience 是对这份工作有用的经验。

normal.en: The opposite is irrelevant, the prefix marking the absence.
normal.cn: 反义词是 irrelevant，前缀标记「没有」。

normal.en: The noun is relevance, the quality of fitting the matter.
normal.cn: 名词是 relevance，即切合这件事的性质。

normal.en: Relevant is not from relate, though the two look alike.
normal.cn: relevant 并非出自 relate，尽管两者形似。

abstract.en: A fact is not relevant in itself; it is relevant to a question.
abstract.cn: 事实本身并无相关性，它只相对于某个问题才相关。

abstract.en: To stay relevant is to keep answering questions people still ask.
abstract.cn: 保持切题，就是持续回答人们仍在问的问题。

abstract.en: The skill of thinking is largely the skill of discarding what is irrelevant.
abstract.cn: 思考的本领，很大程度上是丢掉无关之物的本领。

examples.en: Only the facts relevant to the case were read aloud.
examples.cn: 只有与本案相关的事实被朗读出来。

examples.en: Her question was short but highly relevant to the decision.
examples.cn: 她的问题很短，却与这项决定高度相关。

examples.en: He listed the skills relevant to the job in one short paragraph.
examples.cn: 他用一小段话列出了与这份工作相关的技能。

dict_mnemonic.text: re（往回、向上）加 lev（举起）加 ant：被举到讨论中央、能撑起这个问题的，就是「相关的、切题的」。

root: 拉丁 levis（轻的）→ levare（举起、使轻）→ relevare（举起、减轻、援助）→ relevans（帮助的）→ 法语 relevant → 英语 relevant；出自 lev- 词族，与 relate/relation 的 referre 词族不同源。同族有 relevance、irrelevant。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what bears on the matter; the senses move from a direct connection to usefulness and weight.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「压在议题上」；义项从直接的联系，到有用与有分量。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a few pages pulled out of a thick file and set in the middle of the table.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠材料里只有几页被抽出来放到桌子中央。

branches.en: facts tied to one case
branches.cn: 与一个案件相连的事实

branches.en: a short question that decides
branches.cn: 一个决定走向的短问题

branches.en: connected and also weighty
branches.cn: 既相连又有分量

branches.en: a paragraph that answers the advert
branches.cn: 回答了招聘要求的一段话

branches.en: a page kept and a page set aside
branches.cn: 留下的一页与放到一边的一页

intro.en: A Latin verb of lifting becomes a participle of helping, and the participle names what is worth bringing into a discussion.
intro.cn: 拉丁语表「举起」的动词变成表「帮助」的分词，这个分词便命名值得被带进讨论的东西。

latinIntro.en: The base is levare, to lift, from levis, light; re- adds force, and -ant forms the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 levare（举起），出自 levis（轻的）；re- 加强语气，-ant 构成形容词。

definition_en: able to be trusted to do what is expected; giving consistent and accurate results
core_image: 同一座石桥几十年里每天承受同样的车流
scene: 河上那座石桥几十年如一日地承受着同样的车流，从没出过事。We need a reliable source before we publish the story.
sceneCN: 这里 reliable 是「可靠的」（第 1 个义项：可以被信赖、按预期行事）；句意为在发表这篇报道之前，我们需要一个可靠的来源。画面里可留意：每天都承受车流的石桥。

senses.title: Able to be trusted
senses.definition: of a person or a thing, able to be depended on to do what is expected
senses.definitionCN: 指人或物能被依靠、按预期行事
senses.example: We need a reliable source before we publish the story.
senses.exampleCN: 在发表这篇报道之前，我们需要一个可靠的来源。
senses.why: The word is rely plus the ending able: what can be relied on is what can be leaned on without its giving way.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是 rely 加上词尾 able：能被 rely 的东西，就是可以靠上去而不塌的东西。

senses.title: Consistent in results
senses.definition: giving the same accurate result each time it is used
senses.definitionCN: 每次使用都给出同样准确的结果
senses.example: The old scale is not reliable enough for the laboratory.
senses.exampleCN: 这台旧天平对实验室来说不够可靠。
senses.why: Trust in a machine is trust in repetition: the same result, again and again, without surprise.
senses.whyCN: 对机器的信任是对重复的信任：同样的结果一次次出现，没有意外。

intro.en: Reliable is rely plus able; rely itself goes back to a Latin verb meaning to bind fast, so the image is of something tied and able to hold.
intro.cn: reliable 是 rely 加 able；rely 本身可追到一个意为「绑紧」的拉丁动词，意象是被系住并能承重的东西。

items.en: Ligare meant to tie or bind, the root of ligament and of the relig- family.
items.cn: ligare 意为捆绑，是 ligament 与 relig- 词族的根。

items.en: Religare joined re-, back or fast, with ligare and meant to bind tightly.
items.cn: religare 由 re-（往回、紧紧地）与 ligare 组合，意为紧紧绑住。

items.en: Old French relier meant to bind together or to attach, and English borrowed it as rely.
items.cn: 古法语 relier 意为绑在一起或系上，英语借入后成为 rely。

items.en: English rely first meant to gather together, then to depend on a person or a thing.
items.cn: 英语 rely 最初意为聚拢，后来意为依靠某人或某物。

items.en: The ending -able turned the verb into an adjective of capacity: able to be relied on.
items.cn: 词尾 -able 把这个动词变成表能力的形容词：可以被依靠的。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words of the same binding stem; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives of trustworthiness.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「捆绑」词干的词；近义组收表示可信赖的形容词。

entries.definition: To depend on someone or something.
The state of depending on something.

normalIntro.en: The word is able to be tied to: what is reliable holds when you lean your weight on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「可以被系住的」：可靠的东西，在你把重量压上去时能撑住。

normal.en: Rely plus able: able to be depended on.
normal.cn: rely 加 able：可以被依靠的。

normal.en: A reliable source is one that has never had to be corrected.
normal.cn: a reliable source 是从来不需要更正的那种来源。

normal.en: A reliable car starts on cold mornings.
normal.cn: a reliable car 在寒冷的早晨也能发动。

normal.en: Reliability is measured over time, not in one good day.
normal.cn: 可靠性要靠时间衡量，不是靠一天的好表现。

normal.en: Ligare means to bind, and what is bound does not come apart.
normal.cn: ligare 意为捆绑，被绑住的东西不会散开。

abstract.en: Reliability is a promise kept more than once.
abstract.cn: 可靠，是被遵守了不止一次的承诺。

abstract.en: We trust machines for their repetition and people for their judgement.
abstract.cn: 我们因机器的重复而信任它，因人的判断而信任人。

abstract.en: A reliable witness is rarer than a loud one.
abstract.cn: 可靠的证人比声音大的证人更少见。

examples.en: We need a reliable source before we publish the story.
examples.cn: 在发表这篇报道之前，我们需要一个可靠的来源。

examples.en: The old scale is not reliable enough for the laboratory.
examples.cn: 这台旧天平对实验室来说不够可靠。

examples.en: She is the most reliable member of the night shift.
examples.cn: 她是夜班中最可靠的一员。

dict_mnemonic.text: rely（绑紧、依靠）加 able（能够）：能被系住、能靠上去的，就是可靠的。

root: 拉丁 ligare（捆绑）→ religare（紧紧绑住）→ 古法语 relier（绑在一起）→ 英语 rely（依靠）＋ -able → reliable；同族有 reliance、reliability、reliably，形近的 ligament 也出自 ligare。

sensesIntro.en: The core is being able to be leaned on; the senses move from a trusted person or source to a machine that repeats itself exactly.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「可以靠上去」；义项从可信的人或来源，到每次结果都一致的机器。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone bridge carrying the same traffic for decades without a crack.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一座石桥几十年里每天承受同样的车流。

branches.en: a witness who never shifts
branches.cn: 说法从不动摇的证人

branches.en: a scale that gives the same reading
branches.cn: 每次读数相同的天平

branches.en: a person and a machine both predictable
branches.cn: 同样可预期的人与机器

branches.en: a nightly shift that always arrives
branches.cn: 每晚都准时到的人

branches.en: a story held back until it is checked
branches.cn: 核实之前压着不发的报道

intro.en: A Latin verb of binding gives a French verb of attaching, English makes it rely, and the ending of capacity turns it into an adjective of trust.
intro.cn: 拉丁语表「捆绑」的动词给出法语表「系上」的动词，英语把它变成 rely，表能力的词尾再把它变成表信赖的形容词。

latinIntro.en: The base is ligare, to bind; religare means to bind fast, and -able marks what can be done.
latinIntro.cn: 词根是 ligare（捆绑）；religare 意为紧紧绑住，-able 标记「可以被……的」。

definition_zh: 可靠地；稳定地；有把握地；可信地；不出差错地
definition_en: in a way that can be trusted to give accurate, consistent, or dependable results
core_image: 校准台上摆着一排相同的砝码，每次称量，指针都停在同一格刻度上。
scene: 实验室主管让学生把同一份样品连测三次，三次读数几乎分毫不差，她这才同意把数据写进报告。The instrument reliably gave the same reading three times, so the results could be trusted in the report.
sceneCN: 这里 reliably 是“稳定可靠地得出结果”（第 1 个义项）；句意：三次读数一致，结果可信，可以写进报告。

pos.zh: 可靠地；稳定地；有把握地

senses.title: Results you can trust
senses.titleCN: 可靠地：结果经得起信任
senses.definition: in a way that produces results a person can trust without checking every step
senses.definitionCN: 以让人无须逐步核查也能信任其结果的方式
senses.example: The sensor reliably reports the temperature to within half a degree.
senses.exampleCN: 这个传感器能可靠地把温度报告到半度以内。
senses.why: The suffix -ly turns the adjective reliable into a manner; reliable itself comes from rely, to bind fast, so the manner described is one that does not slip.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ly 把形容词 reliable 变成方式副词；reliable 出自 rely“牢牢绑住”，因此这种做事方式不会松脱走样。

senses.title: The same every time
senses.titleCN: 稳定重现：每次都是同一个结果
senses.definition: in a way that repeats the same outcome under the same conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在相同条件下重复得出同一结果的方式
senses.example: The recipe reliably produces the same crumb every time she bakes it.
senses.exampleCN: 她每次烘烤，这个配方都稳定地做出同样的组织。
senses.why: Repetition is the practical test of reliability: if the outcome moves about, the method cannot be trusted, however good a single trial looks.
senses.whyCN: 重复是可靠性的实际检验：结果若飘忽不定，方法就不可信，单次试验再漂亮也没有用。

senses.title: Machines that do not fail
senses.titleCN: 不出差错地：设备与服务靠得住
senses.definition: with a low rate of failure, especially of machines, systems, or services
senses.definitionCN: 故障率很低，尤指机器、系统或服务
senses.example: The backup generator has run reliably through three winter storms.
senses.exampleCN: 这台备用发电机经历了三场冬季风暴，一直运行可靠。
senses.why: When the subject is a machine, reliability is counted in hours of service rather than in truth; -ly still marks the manner of working.
senses.whyCN: 主语是机器时，可靠性以服务时长而不是以真假来衡量；-ly 标记的仍是运行的方式。

senses.title: A source worth believing
senses.titleCN: 有把握地：消息来源可信
senses.definition: in a way that shows the speaker has sound grounds for what is said
senses.definitionCN: 表现出说话者对所言有可靠依据的方式
senses.example: She is reliably informed that the talks will resume next month.
senses.exampleCN: 据她可靠的消息，会谈将于下月恢复。
senses.why: The phrase reliably informed moves the word from things to testimony: reliability now belongs to the channel that supplies the news.
senses.whyCN: reliably informed 把词从“事物”移到“证言”：这里的可靠性属于提供消息的那个渠道。

senses.title: Measured with little error
senses.definition: with a small margin of error when a value is measured or estimated
senses.definitionCN: 测量或估计数值时误差很小
senses.example: Satellite data can reliably estimate the area of open water.
senses.exampleCN: 卫星数据能可靠地估算开阔水域的面积。
senses.why: Accuracy is closeness to a true value; reliability is getting that closeness again and again. The adverb often carries both at once.
senses.whyCN: 准确讲的是与真值接近，可靠讲的是能否一次次保持这种接近；这个副词常常两者兼有。

senses.title: Predictable in advance
senses.titleCN: 可预期地：事先就能算准
senses.definition: in a way that allows an outcome to be forecast before it happens
senses.definitionCN: 使结果能在发生之前就被预测的方式
senses.example: Demand for electricity reliably peaks on the hottest afternoons.
senses.exampleCN: 用电需求可靠地在最热的下午达到高峰。
senses.why: A pattern that can be counted on becomes a planning tool; predictability is reliability seen from the future looking back.
senses.whyCN: 能被指望的规律就成了规划工具；可预测性是从未来往回看的可靠性。

senses.title: Holding up over time
senses.definition: continuing to work well over a long period without sudden loss of quality
senses.definitionCN: 长时间持续良好运转，质量不突然下滑
senses.example: The bridge has carried traffic reliably for over eighty years.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥已可靠地承载交通八十余年。
senses.why: Durability adds a time axis: a thing may work well today yet be unreliable if it fails soon, so the adverb claims endurance.
senses.whyCN: 耐久性加上了时间轴：某物今天好用，若不久就坏仍不可靠；这个副词主张的是持久。

senses.title: Safely assumed in reasoning
senses.titleCN: 可信地：推理中可当前提
senses.definition: used to say that something may be taken as true in an argument
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示在某论证中可以把某事当作真的
senses.example: We can reliably assume that any sample drawn this way is unbiased.
senses.exampleCN: 我们可以可信地假定，这样抽取的样本没有偏差。
senses.why: In logic the adverb licenses an inference rather than describing an action; reliability means the premise will not betray the conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 在逻辑里这个副词是给推理发放许可，而不是描述动作；可靠意味着前提不会让结论落空。

intro.en: Reliably is rely plus -able plus -ly. The Latin source is religare, to bind fast, whose participle gave the idea of something tied so that it cannot slip.
intro.cn: reliably 由 rely 加 -able 再加 -ly 构成。其拉丁来源是 religare“牢牢绑住”，其分词义带来“绑紧而不松脱”的观念。

items.en: Ligare meant to tie or bind. A thing bound fast stays where it is put, and this physical image later supplies the moral idea of trust.
items.cn: ligare 意为“系、绑”。绑紧的东西会留在原处，这个具体形象后来提供了“信任”这一抽象含义。

items.en: Religare strengthened the image to binding fast or tying back. Roman writers used it for obligations that hold a person to a duty.
items.cn: religare 把形象加强为“绑牢、系回”。罗马作家用它指把人系在义务上的约束。

items.en: Old French relier meant to fasten together or connect, and it carried both the physical and the binding-obligation senses.
items.cn: 古法语 relier 意为“把……系在一起、连接”，兼有物理捆绑与义务约束两层意思。

items.en: English rely first meant to gather or assemble, then to depend on a person or thing, since what is fastened to you is what you lean on.
items.cn: 英语 rely 最初指“聚集、集合”，后指“依靠人或物”，因为系在你身上的东西正是你所倚靠的。

items.en: The Latin suffix -abilis marked what can be done or what deserves to be done; added to rely it yields reliable, worthy of being depended on.
items.cn: 拉丁后缀 -abilis 标记“可以……的、值得……的”；加在 rely 上得到 reliable“值得依靠的”。

items.en: The Old English adverb ending -lice became -ly. It converts the adjective into the manner of doing something, hence reliably, in a dependable manner.
items.cn: 古英语副词词尾 -lice 演变为 -ly，把形容词转成做事的方式，于是 reliably 就是“以可依靠的方式”。

note.en: The first group is the rely family, which shares one root; the second compares adverbs of dependability, accuracy, and consistency.
note.cn: 第一组是 rely 词族，共享同一词根；第二组比较表示可靠、准确、稳定的几个副词。

entries.definition: to depend on someone or something for support or truth. It names the act of leaning on a source.
entries.definitionCN: 依靠某人或某物以获得支持或真相；命名的是倚靠这一动作。

entries.definition: deserving to be depended on. It judges a person, machine, or result, not a manner.
entries.definitionCN: 值得依靠的；评判的是人、机器或结果，而不是做事方式。

entries.definition: the quality of being dependable, often measured by failure rate or repeatability.
entries.definitionCN: 可靠的性质，常用故障率或可重复性来衡量。

entries.definition: the state of depending on something. It stresses dependence, not the quality of the depended-on thing.
entries.definitionCN: 依赖的状态；强调依赖关系，而不是被依赖物的品质。

entries.definition: in a way that can be counted on, with emphasis on personal or contractual trust.
entries.definitionCN: 可以被指望地；强调人身上的信任或契约上的信守。

entries.definition: in the same way on different occasions, with emphasis on uniformity rather than on truth.
entries.definitionCN: 在不同场合以同样的方式；强调一致性，而不是正确性。

entries.definition: without error, with emphasis on closeness to a true value rather than on repeatability.
entries.definitionCN: 没有错误地；强调与真值的接近，而不是可重复性。

entries.definition: at a regular, unbroken rate. It describes rhythm and continuity rather than trustworthiness.
entries.definitionCN: 以规则、不间断的速度；描述节奏与连续性，而非可信程度。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: rely, -able, -ly. Nothing is added that the word does not contain.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：rely、-able、-ly，不额外添加词里没有的东西。

normal.en: Rely plus able plus ly: able to be relied on, and doing things that way.
normal.cn: 依靠加“能够”再加副词尾：能够被依靠，并且以那种方式做事。

normal.en: A rope tied fast does not slide; that picture is the whole of reliability.
normal.cn: 绑紧的绳子不会滑；这幅画面就是“可靠”的全部内容。

normal.en: Three identical readings are what let a scientist say the method works reliably.
normal.cn: 三次读数一样，科学家才敢说这个方法稳定可靠。

normal.en: In an engineering report, reliably means the part never dropped out of service.
normal.cn: 在工程报告里，可靠就意味着这个零件从未掉过链子。

normal.en: Saying reliably informed puts a guarantee on the messenger as well as the message.
normal.cn: 说“据可靠消息”，等于把消息和传话人一起打了包票。

abstract.en: Reliability is not one success but the willingness to be checked again tomorrow.
abstract.cn: 可靠不是一次成功，而是明天仍敢让别人复查。

abstract.en: Handing a task to a machine moves trust from character to calibration.
abstract.cn: 把任务交给机器，就是把信任从人品转移到刻度。

abstract.en: To call something predictable is to squeeze the future into a number that can be recomputed.
abstract.cn: 说某事可预期，就是把未来压缩成一行可以复算的数。

examples.en: The old pump reliably starts on the first try, even in freezing weather.
examples.cn: 这台旧水泵即使在严寒中也能可靠地一次启动。

examples.en: Studies reliably show that spaced review beats a single long cram.
examples.cn: 研究一致表明，间隔复习胜过一次性长时间突击。

examples.en: A witness who is reliably informed may still repeat a rumour, so the source needs checking.
examples.cn: 消息来源可靠的人也可能转述谣言，因此来源仍需核查。

dict_mnemonic.text: 依赖（rely）加“能够”、加副词尾——能够被依赖地做事，就是可靠地。

root: 由 rely（信赖、依靠，源自拉丁语 religare“牢牢绑住”）加 -able（值得……的）与 -ly（副词后缀）构成，本义为“以牢靠可信、可被依靠的方式”。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of reliably, all circling one idea: what is done this way will not let you down. The thing that holds may be a result, a machine, a source, a measurement, a forecast, a habit, or a premise.
sensesIntro.cn: reliably 的八个义项都围绕一个观念：以这种方式做出的事不会让你落空。靠得住的对象可以是结果、机器、消息来源、测量、预测、习惯，也可以是推理前提。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of identical weights on a calibration bench, the needle stopping at the same mark every time.
core.cn: 核心意象：校准台上一排相同的砝码，指针每次都停在同一格刻度。

chain: RELIABLE ABLE TO BE DEPENDED ON

branches.en: TRUST IN THE RESULT AND IN THE SOURCE: a trustworthy reading and a trustworthy messenger both remove the need for checking.
branches.cn: 信任结果与信任来源：可信的读数和可信的传话人，都免去了逐项核查。

branches.en: REPEATABILITY AND ACCURACY: the same value time after time, and a value close to the true one.
branches.cn: 可重复与精确：一次次得到同一个值，并且这个值贴近真值。

branches.en: ENDURANCE OF THINGS: a machine that does not fail today and a bridge that does not fail for decades.
branches.cn: 事物的耐久：今天不出故障的机器，与几十年不出问题的桥。

branches.en: RELIABILITY SEEN FROM THE FUTURE: a pattern stable enough to plan around.
branches.cn: 从未来看可靠性：稳定到足以据此做计划的规律。

branches.en: RELIABILITY IN ARGUMENT: a premise that will not betray the conclusion drawn from it.
branches.cn: 论证中的可靠性：不会让由它推出的结论落空的前提。

intro.en: Reliably is built from rely plus the adjective suffix -able and the adverb suffix -ly; the family later adds -ability for the abstract quality and un- for the opposite.
intro.cn: reliably 由 rely 加形容词后缀 -able 与副词后缀 -ly 构成；词族后来又用 -ability 表示抽象性质，用 un- 表示相反。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is ligare, to bind, strengthened in religare. The suffix -abilis belongs to Latin adjective formation, while -ly is native English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 ligare“绑”，在 religare 中加强。后缀 -abilis 属拉丁形容词构词，而 -ly 是英语本族词尾。

items.example: The Latin verb survives mainly inside compounds such as oblige and religion.
items.exampleCN: 这个拉丁动词主要残存在 oblige（使负有义务）、religion（宗教）等复合词里。

items.meaning: to bind fast, to tie back
items.example: Roman law spoke of obligations that religare a person to a promise.
items.exampleCN: 罗马法谈到把人系在承诺上的义务，就用这个动词。

items.meaning: to depend on for support or truth
items.example: Readers rely on the glossary when the text turns technical.
items.exampleCN: 文本变得专业时，读者会依靠术语表。

items.example: The clinic needs a reliable supply of clean water.
items.exampleCN: 诊所需要可靠的洁净水供应。

items.example: Engineers test reliability by running the unit for thousands of hours.
items.exampleCN: 工程师通过让设备运行数千小时来测试可靠性。

items.example: The village's reliance on one well made every drought a crisis.
items.exampleCN: 全村依赖一口井，使每次干旱都成了危机。

items.example: The ferry reliably crosses the strait twice a day.
items.exampleCN: 渡轮每天可靠地穿越海峡两次。

items.meaning: not able to be depended on
items.example: An unreliable narrator makes the reader doubt every fact.
items.exampleCN: 不可靠的叙述者让读者怀疑每一个事实。

items.meaning: able to act without depending on others
items.example: The course aims to make students self-reliant in research.
items.exampleCN: 这门课旨在让学生在研究中能够自立。

latinEntries.meaning: able to be, worthy of being

definition_zh: 遗物；遗迹；圣髑；遗风；残存物
definition_en: an object or custom that has survived from an earlier time, especially one kept for its age, holiness or historical value
core_image: 一座废弃教堂的墙角还立着半截石柱，周围是新盖的楼，只有它停在旧年代里
scene: 山间小教堂的祭坛上放着一只旧木匣，匣里是一块据说是古代圣徒的遗骨。On the altar of the mountain chapel lies an old wooden casket holding a relic said to be the bone of an ancient saint.
sceneCN: 这里 relic 指「因年代久远或神圣性而被保存下来的遗物」（第 3 个义项：宗教传统中被尊崇的圣髑）；句意为小教堂祭坛上的木匣里存放着一块据称属于古代圣徒的遗骨。可辨识物件：木匣、祭坛布、烛台、石墙、铁锁。

pos.zh: 遗物；遗迹；圣髑；遗风；残存物

collocations.zh: 过去的遗物；旧时代的残留

senses.title: An object surviving from the past
senses.titleCN: 遗物：从过去留存下来的物件
senses.definition: a thing that has survived from an earlier period and is valued for that survival
senses.definitionCN: 从更早时期留存下来、并因留存本身而受珍视的东西
senses.example: The sword is the last relic of the old castle.
senses.exampleCN: 这把剑是那座古堡最后的遗物。
senses.why: Relic comes from Latin reliquiae, the things left behind, from relinquere, to leave behind; the word begins with a departure.
senses.whyCN: relic 出自拉丁 reliquiae「留下之物」，源于 relinquere「留在身后」；这个词的起点就是一场离去。

senses.title: A ruin of an old structure
senses.titleCN: 遗迹：旧建筑的残存部分
senses.definition: a remaining part of a building or place from an earlier age
senses.definitionCN: 更早时代的建筑或场所残存下来的部分
senses.example: A single arch is the only relic of the abbey.
senses.exampleCN: 一座孤拱是这座修道院仅存的遗迹。
senses.why: A building leaves fragments behind when it falls; those fragments are literally what remains, so the same noun covers stone as well as portable objects.
senses.whyCN: 建筑倒塌时会留下碎片；这些碎片字面上就是「留下的东西」，因此同一个名词既指石块，也指可携带的物件。

senses.title: A sacred bodily remnant
senses.titleCN: 圣髑：宗教中被尊崇的遗骨或遗物
senses.definition: a part of a saint's body or a object connected with a holy person, kept for veneration
senses.definitionCN: 圣徒身体的一部分或与其相关的物品，保存以供敬礼
senses.example: Pilgrims travelled for weeks to see the relic.
senses.exampleCN: 朝圣者走了数周，只为看一眼这件圣髑。
senses.why: In religious use the left-behind object is specifically what death left: bone, cloth or a possession, and the value comes from contact with the holy person.
senses.whyCN: 在宗教用法中，留下的东西具体指死亡留下的部分：骨骸、衣物或随身物；价值来自与圣人的接触。

senses.title: A surviving custom or idea
senses.titleCN: 遗风：旧习俗或旧观念的残存
senses.definition: a practice or belief that continues from an earlier era although its original setting has gone
senses.definitionCN: 从更早时代延续下来、而原初环境已消失的做法或观念
senses.example: The rule is a relic of a time when horses set the speed of travel.
senses.exampleCN: 这条规定是马车决定出行速度那个时代的遗风。
senses.why: Once the word means what is left after something ends, it can name customs as easily as stones: the institution ended, the habit stayed.
senses.whyCN: 一旦这个词指某事物结束后的残留，它就能像指石头一样指习俗：制度终结了，习惯还留着。

senses.title: A personal keepsake
senses.titleCN: 纪念物：与逝者或往事相关的私人物品
senses.definition: an object kept for its connection with a person or period, often of little material value
senses.definitionCN: 因与某人或某段时期有关而保存的物品，常无多少物质价值
senses.example: She kept the old ticket as a relic of their first meeting.
senses.exampleCN: 她把那张旧车票留作他们初次见面的纪念物。
senses.why: The religious sense strips its holiness and leaves the structure: an object that carries contact with an absent person.
senses.whyCN: 去掉神圣性之后，宗教义的结构仍然在：一件承载着与不在场者之接触的物品。

senses.title: An antique or curiosity
senses.titleCN: 古董：因年代而被收藏的旧物
senses.definition: an old object collected or traded for its age and rarity
senses.definitionCN: 因年代与稀有而被收藏或交易的旧物
senses.example: The shop sells relics of the steam age.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店出售蒸汽时代的旧物。
senses.why: Market value attaches to age, so a relic becomes a category of goods; the word now labels a trade as well as a devotion.
senses.whyCN: 市场把价值附着在年代上，于是 relic 成为一种货品类别；这个词既标记虔敬，也标记买卖。

senses.title: Remains of a dead person
senses.titleCN: 遗骸：逝者留下的身体部分
senses.definition: the bodily remains of a dead person, usually in the plural relics or remains
senses.definitionCN: 逝者留下的身体部分，通常用复数 relics 或 remains
senses.example: The relics were buried again after the excavation.
senses.exampleCN: 发掘结束后，遗骸被重新安葬。
senses.why: This is the plainest reading of what is left behind: the body itself, which is why the plural form often appears in burial accounts.
senses.whyCN: 这是「留下之物」最朴素的读法：身体本身，因此复数形式常出现在安葬记述中。

senses.title: Something hopelessly outdated
senses.titleCN: 过时之物：被时代甩下的东西
senses.definition: a person, rule or device regarded as absurdly out of date
senses.definitionCN: 被视为荒唐过时的人、规定或装置
senses.example: The fax machine is a relic in most offices.
senses.exampleCN: 在多数办公室里，传真机已是过时之物。
senses.why: Survival can also be an accusation: if only the obsolete survives, the survivor becomes evidence of decay rather than of value.
senses.whyCN: 留存也可以成为一种指控：若只有被淘汰者留下，留存者就成了衰败的证据，而非价值的证据。

intro.en: Relic reached English through Old French from Latin reliquiae, the things left behind, a plural noun from relinquere, to leave behind. The religious sense came first in English use. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: relic 经古法语来自拉丁 reliquiae「留下之物」，这是由 relinquere「留在身后」派生的复数名词。英语中最早出现的是宗教义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Relinquere means to leave behind or abandon, built from re-, back, and linquere, to leave; its participle reliquus means left over.
items.cn: relinquere 意为留在身后或舍弃，由 re-「向后」与 linquere「离开」构成；其分词 reliquus 意为剩下的。

items.en: The plural reliquiae named what remains after a person or thing is gone, and in church Latin it specialised to the bodily remains of a saint.
items.cn: 复数 reliquiae 指人或物消失后留下的东西，在教会拉丁语中专门指圣徒的遗骸。

items.en: Old French relique carried the devotional sense into English after the Norman period, and the plural relics covered bones, cloth and associated objects.
items.cn: 古法语 relique 在诺曼时期之后把敬礼义带入英语，复数 relics 涵盖骨骸、衣物与相关物品。

items.en: From the sixteenth century the word widened to ruins, surviving customs and old objects in general, while the sacred sense stayed alive.
items.cn: 十六世纪起，这个词扩展到废墟、残存习俗与一般旧物，同时神圣义仍然存活。

items.en: Source uncertain: the deeper origin of linquere is not established beyond the Latin family, and the competing link to a Greek verb meaning to leave is a hypothesis rather than a demonstrated relation.
items.cn: 来源不确定：linquere 在拉丁语族之外的更深来源未有定论；把它与某个意为「离开」的希腊动词相联系的另一种说法只是假说，并非已证实的关联。

note.en: The first group holds words that look or sound close and share the leaving-behind idea; the second group holds nouns for old surviving things.
note.cn: 第一组是形音相近、并共享「留下」观念的单词；第二组是指旧日留存物的名词。

entries.definition: A technical term for a species or feature surviving from an earlier environment; relic is the everyday word for the object.
entries.definitionCN: 指从更早环境残存下来的物种或地貌的技术术语；relic 是日常指物件的词。

entries.definition: The verb built on the same linquere, meaning to give up or let go; a relic is what was relinquished.
entries.definitionCN: 同出 linquere 的动词，意为放弃或放手；遗物就是被放手的东西。

entries.definition: From de- plus relinquere, meaning wholly abandoned; it describes the state, not the surviving object.
entries.definitionCN: 由 de- 加 relinquere 构成，意为被彻底弃置；它描述状态，而非留存物。

entries.definition: The general plural for whatever is left of a body, building or meal; relic usually adds age or reverence.
entries.definitionCN: 泛指身体、建筑或饭菜剩下的部分；relic 通常额外带有年代或敬意。

entries.definition: An object kept to remember a person or event; it stresses the memory, not the survival.
entries.definitionCN: 为记住某人或某事而保存的物品；它强调记忆，而非留存。

entries.definition: An old object valued in the market for its age; the word implies commerce, while relic implies devotion or history.
entries.definitionCN: 因年代在市场上受重视的旧物；该词含买卖意味，而 relic 含虔敬或历史意味。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the leaving-behind verb, the church sense, the ruins and the modern insult.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：表示「留下」的动词、教会义、废墟义，以及现代的贬义。

normal.en: relinquere, to leave behind, gives reliquiae, the things left behind: a relic is a left-behind thing.
normal.cn: relinquere「留在身后」派生 reliquiae「留下之物」：relic 就是被留下的东西。

normal.en: The first English sense was devotional: bones, cloth and possessions of a saint.
normal.cn: 英语最早的义项是宗教性的：圣徒的骨骸、衣物与随身物。

normal.en: The plural relics covers both holy objects and human remains.
normal.cn: 复数 relics 既指神圣物件，也指人的遗骸。

normal.en: A ruin is a relic of a building; a custom can be a relic of an institution.
normal.cn: 废墟是建筑的遗物；习俗可以是某个制度的遗风。

normal.en: Calling a device a relic is an insult about its age, not praise for its survival.
normal.cn: 把某装置称作 relic，是在讥其老旧，而不是赞美它留存下来。

abstract.en: Abstractly, a relic is proof that a departure happened: the object marks an absence.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，遗物是「离去曾发生」的证明：物件标记着一处缺席。

abstract.en: Value attaches to the link, not the material: a bone and a stone differ only in who touched them.
abstract.cn: 价值附着在联系上，而不在材料上：一块骨与一块石，差别只在谁曾触碰过。

abstract.en: Every survival carries a question: is this kept because it still works, or only because it is old?
abstract.cn: 每一种留存都带来一个问题：它被留着是因为仍然有用，还是只因它够老？

examples.en: The mosaics are the finest relic of the settlement's wealthy period.
examples.cn: 这些镶嵌画是该聚落富庶时期最精美的遗物。

examples.en: The procession carries the relic through the streets once a year.
examples.cn: 每年一次，游行队伍抬着这件圣髑穿过街道。

examples.en: Many archaeologists treat such rules as relics of an older recording system.
examples.cn: 许多考古学者把这类规定视为旧记录体系的残留。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「re（回）+ lic（留下）」——人走了，东西留在原地 → 遗物、遗迹

root: 拉丁 relinquere「留在身后」的派生名词 reliquiae「留下之物」，经古法语 relique 进入英语；词根 linquere 意为「离开」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one departure: what is left behind may be an object, a ruin, a saint's bone, a custom, a keepsake, a curiosity, a body or an absurdly outdated thing.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一场离去展开：留下的可以是物件、废墟、圣人骨骸、习俗、纪念物、古董、遗体，或一件荒唐过时的东西。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a departure, and one object still standing where the person used to be.
core.cn: 核心意象：一场离去，以及原来有人之处仍立着的一件物件。

branches.en: THE LEFT-BEHIND THING: portable objects and standing ruins are both simply what the past did not take away.
branches.cn: 留下之物：可携带的物件与仍立的废墟，都只是过去没有带走的东西。

branches.en: CONTACT WITH THE ABSENT: a saint's bone and a body both keep the person present through matter.
branches.cn: 与缺席者的接触：圣徒的骨与遗体都借物质让人继续在场。

branches.en: THE HABIT OUTLASTS THE INSTITUTION: customs remain after the world that made them is gone.
branches.cn: 习惯比制度活得久：造出习俗的世界消失后，习俗仍在。

branches.en: KEEPING AND TRADING: the same old object can be a private memory or a priced curiosity.
branches.cn: 保存与买卖：同一件旧物既可以是私人记忆，也可以是被标价的古董。

branches.en: SURVIVAL AS INSULT: what outlives its use turns from treasure into evidence of decay.
branches.cn: 留存成为讥讽：活得超过用途的东西，从珍宝变成衰败的证据。

intro.en: Relic is a single Latin-derived noun whose stem also builds a small family of English words about leaving things behind.
intro.cn: relic 是一个拉丁来源的名词，其词干还构成一小族表示「留下」的英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin relinquere, to leave behind, yields reliquiae and its English descendants relic and relics, plus relinquish and derelict, which keep the verbal force of leaving.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 relinquere「留在身后」派生 reliquiae，其英语后裔有 relic、relics，以及保留「离开」动词力量的 relinquish 与 derelict。

items.example: The prefix marks motion away and back in many Latin verbs.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀在许多拉丁动词中标记离开与返回的运动。

items.example: Linquere is the root of relinquish and derelict.
items.exampleCN: linquere 是 relinquish 与 derelict 的词根。

items.example: The army relinquished the fort at dawn.
items.exampleCN: 军队在黎明时弃守了堡垒。

items.example: Reliquiae covered bones, ruins and leftovers alike.
items.exampleCN: reliquiae 兼指骨骸、废墟与剩余物。

items.example: The relic was catalogued as twelfth-century work.
items.exampleCN: 这件遗物被编目为十二世纪的作品。

items.example: The relics were reburied with ceremony.
items.exampleCN: 遗骸被以仪式重新安葬。

items.meaning: a species or feature surviving from an earlier age
items.meaningCN: 从更早时代残存的物种或地貌
items.example: The lake holds relict species from the ice age.
items.exampleCN: 这座湖中有冰期残遗物种。

items.meaning: to give up or let go
items.example: She relinquished her claim to the land.
items.exampleCN: 她放弃了对这块土地的主张。

items.example: The derelict warehouse became a studio.
items.exampleCN: 那座废弃仓库变成了工作室。

items.meaning: a container for a sacred relic
items.example: The reliquary is kept in the cathedral treasury.
items.exampleCN: 这只圣髑匣保存在主教座堂的宝库里。
